package main

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"path/filepath"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/google/uuid"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/node"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/codeexec"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/relay"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/remoteshell"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/transport"
)

func main() {
	nodeID := flag.String("id", "", "Unique node identifier (default: generated UUID)")
	poolID := flag.String("pool", "default-pool", "Storage pool identifier")
	storageDir := flag.String("storage", "", "Storage directory for chunk blobs (default: ./unicompute_data)")
	quotaGB := flag.Int64("quota-gb", 10, "Contributed storage quota in GiB")
	signalingURL := flag.String("signaling", "ws://127.0.0.1:8080/ws", "Coordinator signaling WebSocket URL")
	authToken := flag.String("auth-token", os.Getenv("UNICOMPUTE_AUTH_TOKEN"), "Coordinator signaling authentication token")
	enableRemoteShell := flag.Bool("enable-remote-shell", false, "Enable remote shell execution on this node (requires allowlist)")
	shellAllowlist := flag.String("shell-allowlist", "", "Comma-separated peer IDs allowed to execute remote shell commands")
	stunServer := flag.String("stun", "stun.l.google.com:19302", "STUN server address (comma-separated for multiple)")
	stunServer6 := flag.String("stun6", "", "IPv6 STUN server address (comma-separated for multiple)")
	turnServer := flag.String("turn", "", "TURN server address (e.g., turn:relay.example.com:3478, comma-separated for multiple)")
	turnUser := flag.String("turn-user", "", "TURN server username")
	turnCred := flag.String("turn-cred", "", "TURN server credential / password")
	relayAddr := flag.String("relay", "", "Contributor relay address (deprecated: use TURN for NAT relay fallback)")
	runRelay := flag.Bool("run-relay", false, "Contribute relay bandwidth to the fleet (deprecated: use embedded/external TURN)")
	enableCodeExecution := flag.Bool("enable-code-execution", false, "Enable Docker sandbox code execution on this worker")
	codeAllowlist := flag.String("code-allowlist", "", "Comma-separated node IDs allowed to submit code jobs")
	codeTimeout := flag.Int("code-timeout", 10, "Code job timeout in seconds (1-30)")
	relayListen := flag.String("relay-listen", "0.0.0.0:22067", "Relay listen address if run-relay is enabled")
	enableGPU := flag.Bool("enable-gpu", false, "Enable Objective 3 GPU acceleration and resource governance")
	gpuBackend := flag.String("gpu-backend", "auto", "Preferred GPU compute backend: auto, directml, cuda")
	gpuMemLimitMB := flag.Int("gpu-mem-limit-mb", 2048, "GPU process memory ceiling in MB")
	gpuWatchdogPollMS := flag.Int("gpu-watchdog-poll-ms", 50, "Watchdog polling frequency in ms (default: 50)")
	gpuIgnoreBattery := flag.Bool("gpu-ignore-battery", false, "Ignore battery state (for testing or plugged-in lab machines)")

	flag.Parse()
	if *codeTimeout < 1 || *codeTimeout > codeexec.MaxTimeoutSeconds {
		log.Fatalf("-code-timeout must be between 1 and %d seconds", codeexec.MaxTimeoutSeconds)
	}

	if *enableRemoteShell && strings.TrimSpace(*shellAllowlist) == "" {
		log.Fatalf("[FATAL] -enable-remote-shell is true but -shell-allowlist is empty; remote shell startup refused for security")
	}

	var shellList []string
	if *shellAllowlist != "" {
		for _, s := range strings.Split(*shellAllowlist, ",") {
			s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
			if s != "" {
				shellList = append(shellList, s)
			}
		}
	}

	if *nodeID == "" {
		*nodeID = "node-" + uuid.New().String()[:8]
	}

	if *storageDir == "" {
		home, err := os.UserHomeDir()
		if err != nil {
			home = "."
		}
		*storageDir = filepath.Join(home, ".unicompute", "storage", *nodeID)
	}

	var stunListV4 []string
	if *stunServer != "" {
		for _, s := range strings.Split(*stunServer, ",") {
			s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
			if s != "" {
				stunListV4 = append(stunListV4, s)
			}
		}
	}

	var stunListV6 []string
	if *stunServer6 != "" {
		for _, s := range strings.Split(*stunServer6, ",") {
			s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
			if s != "" {
				stunListV6 = append(stunListV6, s)
			}
		}
	}

	var turnConfigs []transport.TURNServerConfig
	if *turnServer != "" {
		for _, s := range strings.Split(*turnServer, ",") {
			s = strings.TrimSpace(s)
			if s != "" {
				turnConfigs = append(turnConfigs, transport.TURNServerConfig{
					URL:        s,
					Username:   *turnUser,
					Credential: *turnCred,
				})
			}
		}
	}

	fmt.Println("===================================================================")
	fmt.Println(" UniCompute Objective 1: Peer-to-Peer Storage Substrate")
	fmt.Printf(" Node ID:        %s\n", *nodeID)
	fmt.Printf(" Pool ID:        %s\n", *poolID)
	fmt.Printf(" Storage Quota:  %d GiB\n", *quotaGB)
	fmt.Printf(" Storage Path:   %s\n", *storageDir)
	fmt.Printf(" Signaling URL:  %s\n", *signalingURL)
	if len(stunListV4) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf(" STUN Server(s): %s\n", strings.Join(stunListV4, ", "))
	}
	if len(stunListV6) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf(" STUN IPv6:      %s\n", strings.Join(stunListV6, ", "))
	}
	if len(turnConfigs) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf(" TURN Server(s): %s\n", *turnServer)
	}
	fmt.Println("===================================================================")

	// If runRelay is enabled, start contributor relay
	var contributorRelay *relay.ContributorRelay
	if *runRelay {
		log.Println("[DEPRECATED] -run-relay is deprecated; native Pion WebRTC ICE with embedded/external TURN is preferred.")
		var err error
		contributorRelay, err = relay.NewContributorRelay(relay.ServerConfig{
			ListenAddr:     *relayListen,
			SessionTimeout: 30 * time.Second,
		})
		if err != nil {
			log.Printf("[WARN] Failed to start contributor relay: %v\n", err)
		} else {
			defer contributorRelay.Close()
			log.Printf("[INFO] Contributor relay running on %s\n", contributorRelay.Addr().String())
		}
	} else if *relayAddr != "" {
		log.Println("[DEPRECATED] -relay is deprecated; native Pion WebRTC ICE with embedded/external TURN is preferred.")
	}

	quotaBytes := *quotaGB * 1024 * 1024 * 1024
	n, err := node.NewNode(node.NodeConfig{
		NodeID:            *nodeID,
		PoolID:            *poolID,
		StorageDir:        *storageDir,
		StorageQuota:      quotaBytes,
		SignalingURL:      *signalingURL,
		AuthToken:         *authToken,
		STUNServersV4:     stunListV4,
		STUNServersV6:     stunListV6,
		TURNServers:       turnConfigs,
		RelayAddr:         *relayAddr,
		FallbackTimeout:   2000 * time.Millisecond,
		EnableRemoteShell: *enableRemoteShell,
		ShellAllowlist:    shellList,
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("[FATAL] Failed to initialize node: %v\n", err)
	}
	if *enableCodeExecution {
		var allowedPeers []string
		for _, peerID := range strings.Split(*codeAllowlist, ",") {
			if peerID = strings.TrimSpace(peerID); peerID != "" {
				allowedPeers = append(allowedPeers, peerID)
			}
		}
		if len(allowedPeers) == 0 {
			log.Fatalf("-enable-code-execution requires -code-allowlist with one or more trusted peer IDs")
		}
		dockerCtx, cancelDocker := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
		dockerErr := codeexec.CheckDocker(dockerCtx)
		cancelDocker()
		if dockerErr != nil {
			log.Fatalf("code execution requested but Docker is unavailable: %v", dockerErr)
		}
		n.SetCodeExecutor(codeexec.NewDockerExecutor(codeexec.Config{
			DefaultTimeout: time.Duration(*codeTimeout) * time.Second,
			MaxTimeout:     time.Duration(codeexec.MaxTimeoutSeconds) * time.Second,
			MaxConcurrent:  2,
		}), allowedPeers...)
		log.Printf("[CODEEXEC] Docker sandbox enabled; allowed submitting peers: %s", strings.Join(allowedPeers, ", "))
	}
	if *enableGPU {
		prefBackend := gpu.BackendDirectML
		switch strings.ToLower(*gpuBackend) {
		case "cuda":
			prefBackend = gpu.BackendCUDA
		case "directml":
			prefBackend = gpu.BackendDirectML
		default:
			prefBackend = ""
		}
		gpuCfg := gpu.ManagerConfig{
			StorageDir:          filepath.Join(*storageDir, "gpu"),
			MaxMemoryBytes:      uint64(*gpuMemLimitMB) * 1024 * 1024,
			PreferredBackend:    prefBackend,
			WatchdogInterval:    time.Duration(*gpuWatchdogPollMS) * time.Millisecond,
			UserActiveThreshold: 1000 * time.Millisecond,
			ResumeGracePeriod:   30 * time.Second,
			IgnoreBattery:       *gpuIgnoreBattery,
		}
		if err := n.EnableGPU(gpuCfg); err != nil {
			log.Printf("[WARN] Failed to enable GPU subsystem: %v\n", err)
		} else {
			prof, _ := n.GPUProfile()
			log.Printf("[GPU] Objective 3 enabled: %s (%s, %d MB VRAM, DirectML=%v, CUDA=%v)",
				prof.DeviceName, prof.Vendor, prof.TotalVRAMBytes/(1024*1024), prof.DirectMLSupported, prof.CUDASupported)
		}
	}
	defer n.Close()

	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	defer cancel()

	log.Println("[INFO] Starting node and classifying network topology...")
	if err := n.Start(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[WARN] Node startup note: %v (running in offline/direct mode)\n", err)
	}

	// Print NAT & Network diagnostics
	natRep := n.NATReport()
	if natRep != nil {
		fmt.Println("\n--- Network Diagnostics ---")
		fmt.Printf(" NAT Classification: %s\n", natRep.NATType)
		fmt.Printf(" Behind CGNAT:        %v (RFC 6598 100.64.0.0/10)\n", natRep.IsBehindCGNAT)
		fmt.Printf(" IPv4 Available:      %v (Public: %s)\n", natRep.IPv4Supported, natRep.PublicIPv4)
		fmt.Printf(" IPv6 Available:      %v (Public: %s)\n", natRep.IPv6Supported, natRep.PublicIPv6)
		fmt.Printf(" Hole-Punch Feasible: %v\n", natRep.HolePunchFeasible)
		fmt.Printf(" Requires Relay:      %v\n", natRep.RequiresRelay)
		if len(natRep.FilteredInterfaces) > 0 {
			fmt.Printf(" Pruned Virtual Adapters: %v\n", natRep.FilteredInterfaces)
		}
		fmt.Println("---------------------------")
	}

	// Event hooks
	n.SetOnChunkReceived(func(peerID, chunkID string, size int64) {
		fmt.Printf("\n[EVENT] Chunk %s (%d bytes) received from peer %s and stored\n> ", chunkID, size, peerID)
	})

	n.SetOnStreamMessage(func(peerID string, data []byte) {
		msgStr := string(data)
		if strings.HasPrefix(msgStr, "__PING__:") {
			ts := strings.TrimPrefix(msgStr, "__PING__:")
			_ = n.SendStream(peerID, []byte("__PONG__:"+ts))
			return
		}
		if strings.HasPrefix(msgStr, "__PONG__:") {
			tsStr := strings.TrimPrefix(msgStr, "__PONG__:")
			parts := strings.Split(tsStr, ":")
			if len(parts) > 0 {
				if tsNano, err := strconv.ParseInt(parts[0], 10, 64); err == nil {
					rtt := time.Duration(time.Now().UnixNano() - tsNano)
					fmt.Printf("\n[PONG] Reply from %s: RTT=%.2fms\n> ", peerID, float64(rtt)/float64(time.Millisecond))
					return
				}
			}
			fmt.Printf("\n[PONG] Reply from %s: Pong received!\n> ", peerID)
			return
		}
		fmt.Printf("\n[STREAM] Message from %s: %s\n> ", peerID, msgStr)
	})

	n.SetOnPeerConnected(func(peerID string) {
		fmt.Printf("\n[EVENT] Peer %s connected via WebRTC DataChannel\n", peerID)
		if m, ok := n.GetPathMetrics(peerID); ok {
			fmt.Printf("[METRICS] Peer %s path: direct=%v, pair=%s, local=%s, remote=%s\n> ",
				peerID, m.IsDirect, m.PairType, m.LocalCandidate, m.RemoteCandidate)
		} else {
			fmt.Print("> ")
		}
	})

	n.SetOnFleetPeerJoined(func(peerID string) {
		fmt.Printf("\n[FLEET] Peer '%s' joined the fleet! (Type 'connect %s' to establish P2P link)\n> ", peerID, peerID)
	})

	n.SetOnFleetPeerLeft(func(peerID string) {
		fmt.Printf("\n[FLEET] Peer '%s' disconnected from the fleet.\n> ", peerID)
	})

	// Initial fleet discovery
	fleetNodes, _ := n.GetFleetNodes(context.Background())
	if len(fleetNodes) > 0 {
		fmt.Printf("[FLEET] %d other peer(s) currently online: %v\n", len(fleetNodes), fleetNodes)
	} else {
		fmt.Println("[FLEET] Connected to coordinator. Waiting for other laptops to connect...")
	}

	// Periodic telemetry reporting
	ticker := time.NewTicker(60 * time.Second)
	defer ticker.Stop()
	go func() {
		for {
			select {
			case <-ticker.C:
				usage := n.StorageUsage()
				var pct float64
				if usage.QuotaBytes > 0 {
					pct = (float64(usage.UsedBytes) / float64(usage.QuotaBytes)) * 100
				}
				log.Printf("[STATUS] Storage: %d / %d MB used (%.1f%%) | Blobs: %d\n",
					usage.UsedBytes/(1024*1024), usage.QuotaBytes/(1024*1024), pct, usage.BlobCount)
			case <-ctx.Done():
				return
			}
		}
	}()

	// Interactive Console Loop
	fmt.Println("\nInteractive Mode Active!")
	fmt.Println("Type 'help' to see commands, or Ctrl+C to exit.")
	fmt.Print("> ")

	go func() {
		scanner := bufio.NewScanner(os.Stdin)
		for scanner.Scan() {
			line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
			if line == "" {
				fmt.Print("> ")
				continue
			}
			parts := splitConsoleArgs(line)
			cmd := strings.ToLower(parts[0])

			switch cmd {
			case "help":
				fmt.Println("Available Commands:")
				fmt.Println("  peers, users, nodes            - List all online fleet nodes & active P2P links")
				fmt.Println("  connect <peerID>               - Establish P2P WebRTC link with a peer")
				fmt.Println("  disconnect <peerID>            - Disconnect active P2P link with a peer")
				fmt.Println("  ping <peerID>                  - Ping a connected peer over SCTP stream channel")
				fmt.Println("  stream <peerID> <message>      - Send live stream message/log to a peer")
				fmt.Println("  put <filePath>                 - Store a local file into the disk vault")
				fmt.Println("  get <blobID> [destFile]        - Retrieve and view/export a stored blob")
				fmt.Println("  transfer <peerID> <blobID>     - Transfer a blob to peer over WebRTC")
				fmt.Println("  fetch <peerID> <blobID> [sz]   - Fetch a blob from peer over WebRTC")
				fmt.Println("  list, ls                       - List all stored blobs in the local vault")
				fmt.Println("  stat <blobID>                  - Show metadata for a stored blob")
				fmt.Println("  del <blobID>                   - Delete a stored blob from vault")
				fmt.Println("  scrub                          - Scrub blob store for bitrot")
				fmt.Println("  status, info                   - Display full local node and network status")
				fmt.Println("  metrics                        - Display live path metrics")
				fmt.Println("  nat                            - Show local NAT diagnostics")
				fmt.Println("  exec <peerID|all> <command...> - Execute shell command on connected remote PC(s)")
				fmt.Println("  shell <peerID|all> <cmd...>    - Alias for remote command execution")
				fmt.Println("  run <peerID> <c|cpp|python> <source-file> [stdin-file] - Run source code in a Docker sandbox")
				fmt.Println("  gpu                            - Display GPU hardware profile & watchdog state")
				fmt.Println("  gpu-run <c|cpp|onnx> <file>    - Run GPU workload with Win32 JobObject governance")
				fmt.Println("  hipify <cuda-source-file>      - Analyze CUDA C++ source for AMD compatibility & translate")
				fmt.Println("  quit, exit                     - Terminate the node")
			case "peers", "users", "nodes":
				fleetList, err := n.GetFleetNodes(context.Background())
				connectedPeers := n.GetConnectedPeers()

				connectedMap := make(map[string]bool)
				for _, p := range connectedPeers {
					connectedMap[p] = true
				}

				fmt.Println("\n=================== UniCompute Network Status ===================")
				fmt.Printf(" Local Node ID:  %s\n", *nodeID)
				fmt.Printf(" Signaling URL:  %s\n", *signalingURL)
				fmt.Println("-----------------------------------------------------------------")
				
				fmt.Printf(" Available Fleet Nodes (%d online):\n", len(fleetList))
				if len(fleetList) == 0 {
					fmt.Println("   (No other nodes currently registered with coordinator)")
				} else {
					for _, fn := range fleetList {
						if connectedMap[fn] {
							fmt.Printf("   [*] %s (Connected P2P)\n", fn)
						} else {
							fmt.Printf("   [*] %s (Online on coordinator - type 'connect %s')\n", fn, fn)
						}
					}
				}

				fmt.Println("-----------------------------------------------------------------")
				fmt.Printf(" Active P2P DataChannels (%d connected):\n", len(connectedPeers))
				if len(connectedPeers) == 0 {
					fmt.Println("   (No active P2P links. Connect using 'connect <peerID>')")
				} else {
					for i, p := range connectedPeers {
						pathStr := "P2P DataChannel"
						if m, ok := n.GetPathMetrics(p); ok {
							pathStr = fmt.Sprintf("direct=%v | pair=%s | local=%s | remote=%s",
								m.IsDirect, m.PairType, m.LocalCandidate, m.RemoteCandidate)
						}
						fmt.Printf("   [%d] %s [%s]\n", i+1, p, pathStr)
					}
				}
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf(" [NOTE] Coordinator query note: %v\n", err)
				}
				fmt.Println("=================================================================")
			case "disconnect":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: disconnect <peerID>")
					break
				}
				peerID := parts[1]
				if err := n.DisconnectPeer(peerID); err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Disconnect failed: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Disconnected P2P link with %s.\n", peerID)
				}
			case "ping":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: ping <peerID>")
					break
				}
				peerID := parts[1]
				nowNano := fmt.Sprintf("%d", time.Now().UnixNano())
				pingID := uuid.New().String()[:8]
				if err := n.SendStream(peerID, []byte(fmt.Sprintf("__PING__:%s:%s", nowNano, pingID))); err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Ping failed: %v (are you connected? type 'connect %s')\n", err, peerID)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Ping sent to %s...\n", peerID)
				}
			case "status", "info":
				usage := n.StorageUsage()
				connectedPeers := n.GetConnectedPeers()
				rep := n.NATReport()

				fmt.Println("\n==================== Local Node Diagnostics ====================")
				fmt.Printf(" Node ID:        %s\n", *nodeID)
				fmt.Printf(" Storage Path:   %s\n", *storageDir)
				var pct float64
				if usage.QuotaBytes > 0 {
					pct = (float64(usage.UsedBytes) / float64(usage.QuotaBytes)) * 100
				}
				fmt.Printf(" Storage Quota:  %d MB total | %d MB used (%.1f%%) | %d Blobs\n",
					usage.QuotaBytes/(1024*1024), usage.UsedBytes/(1024*1024), pct, usage.BlobCount)
				fmt.Printf(" Signaling Hub:  %s\n", *signalingURL)
				fmt.Printf(" Connected P2P:  %d peer(s) %v\n", len(connectedPeers), connectedPeers)
				if rep != nil {
					fmt.Printf(" NAT Type:       %s (CGNAT: %v, HolePunch: %v)\n",
						rep.NATType, rep.IsBehindCGNAT, rep.HolePunchFeasible)
				}
				fmt.Println("================================================================")
			case "get":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: get <blobID> [destinationPath]")
					break
				}
				dest := ""
				if len(parts) >= 3 {
					dest = parts[2]
				}
				handleGetBlob(n, parts[1], dest)
			case "fetch":
				if len(parts) < 3 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: fetch <peerID> <blobID> [expectedSize]")
					break
				}
				peerID, blobID := parts[1], parts[2]
				var expectedSize int64
				if len(parts) >= 4 {
					fmt.Sscanf(parts[3], "%d", &expectedSize)
				}
				start := time.Now()
				fetchCtx, cancelFetch := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
				err := n.FetchChunk(fetchCtx, peerID, blobID, expectedSize)
				cancelFetch()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Fetch failed: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Successfully fetched blob %s from %s in %v\n", blobID, peerID, time.Since(start))
				}
			case "put":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: put <filePath>")
					break
				}
				filePath := parts[1]
				f, err := os.Open(filePath)
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Error opening file: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				hasher := sha256.New()
				if _, err := io.Copy(hasher, f); err != nil {
					f.Close()
					fmt.Printf("Error hashing file: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				blobID := hex.EncodeToString(hasher.Sum(nil))
				if _, err := f.Seek(0, io.SeekStart); err != nil {
					f.Close()
					fmt.Printf("Error rewinding file: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				written, err := n.PutBlob(blobID, f)
				f.Close()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("PutBlob failed: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Successfully stored blob: %s (%d bytes)\n", blobID, written)
				}
			case "list", "ls":
				blobs, err := n.ListBlobs()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Error listing blobs: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				fmt.Printf("Stored Blobs in Local Vault (%d total):\n", len(blobs))
				if len(blobs) == 0 {
					fmt.Println("  (Storage vault is currently empty. Use 'put <file>' to store blobs)")
				} else {
					for i, b := range blobs {
						sizeKB := float64(b.Size) / 1024.0
						fmt.Printf("  [%d] ID: %s | Size: %d bytes (%.2f KB) | Mod: %s\n",
							i+1, b.ID, b.Size, sizeKB, b.ModTime.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
					}
				}
			case "stat":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: stat <blobID>")
					break
				}
				info, err := n.StatBlob(parts[1])
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Stat error: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Blob: %s | Size: %d bytes | Mod: %s | SHA256: %s\n", info.ID, info.Size, info.ModTime.Format(time.RFC3339), info.SHA256)
				}
			case "del", "rm":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: del <blobID>")
					break
				}
				if err := n.DeleteBlob(parts[1]); err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Delete error: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Blob %s deleted successfully\n", parts[1])
				}
			case "scrub":
				corrupted, err := n.Scrub()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Scrub error: %v\n", err)
				} else if len(corrupted) == 0 {
					fmt.Println("Scrub complete: all stored blobs passed cryptographic SHA-256 verification.")
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("WARNING: Found %d corrupt blobs: %v\n", len(corrupted), corrupted)
				}
			case "connect":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: connect <peerID>")
					break
				}
				peerID := parts[1]
				fmt.Printf("Establishing WebRTC P2P link with %s...\n", peerID)
				connCtx, cancelConn := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 15*time.Second)
				_, err := n.ConnectPeer(connCtx, peerID)
				cancelConn()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Connection to %s failed: %v\n", peerID, err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("WebRTC DataChannel connected to %s!\n", peerID)
				}
			case "transfer":
				if len(parts) < 3 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: transfer <peerID> <blobID>")
					break
				}
				peerID, blobID := parts[1], parts[2]
				start := time.Now()
				txCtx, cancelTx := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
				err := n.TransferChunk(txCtx, peerID, blobID)
				cancelTx()
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Transfer failed: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Transferred blob %s to %s in %v\n", blobID, peerID, time.Since(start))
				}
			case "stream":
				if len(parts) < 3 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: stream <peerID> <message...>")
					break
				}
				peerID := parts[1]
				msg := strings.Join(parts[2:], " ")
				if err := n.SendStream(peerID, []byte(msg)); err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Stream error: %v\n", err)
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("Stream message sent to %s\n", peerID)
				}
			case "metrics":
				stats := n.FleetStats()
				fmt.Printf("Fleet Metrics: Total=%d | Direct=%d | Relayed=%d | Direct%%=%.1f%% | CGNAT%%=%.1f%%\n",
					stats.TotalConnections, stats.DirectConnections, stats.RelayedConnections, stats.DirectConnectionPct, stats.CGNATPrevalencePct)
			case "nat":
				rep := n.NATReport()
				if rep != nil {
					fmt.Printf("NAT: %s | CGNAT: %v | HolePunchFeasible: %v | IPv4: %s | IPv6: %s\n",
						rep.NATType, rep.IsBehindCGNAT, rep.HolePunchFeasible, rep.PublicIPv4, rep.PublicIPv6)
				}
			case "exec", "shell":
				if len(parts) < 3 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: exec <peerID|all> <command...>")
					fmt.Println("Example: exec node-a1b2 whoami")
					fmt.Println("Example: exec all Get-Process")
					break
				}
				targetPeer := parts[1]
				commandStr := strings.Join(parts[2:], " ")

				if targetPeer == "all" {
					activePeers := n.GetConnectedPeers()
					if len(activePeers) == 0 {
						fmt.Println("[EXEC] No connected remote peers. Establish connection first via 'connect <peerID>'.")
						break
					}
					fmt.Printf("[EXEC] Broadcasting '%s' to %d connected remote peer(s)...\n", commandStr, len(activePeers))
					execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 45*time.Second)
					results := n.ExecuteRemoteCommandAll(execCtx, remoteshell.ShellRequest{
						Command:   commandStr,
						ShellType: remoteshell.ShellAuto,
					})
					cancelExec()

					for pid, res := range results {
						fmt.Println("=================================================================")
						fmt.Printf(" Remote Node: %s | Exit Code: %d | Duration: %d ms\n", pid, res.ExitCode, res.DurationMs)
						if res.Error != "" {
							fmt.Printf(" [!] Error: %s\n", res.Error)
						}
						if res.Stdout != "" {
							fmt.Println(" --- STDOUT ---")
							fmt.Print(res.Stdout)
							if !strings.HasSuffix(res.Stdout, "\n") {
								fmt.Println()
							}
						}
						if res.Stderr != "" {
							fmt.Println(" --- STDERR ---")
							fmt.Print(res.Stderr)
							if !strings.HasSuffix(res.Stderr, "\n") {
								fmt.Println()
							}
						}
						fmt.Println("=================================================================")
					}
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("[EXEC] Executing '%s' on remote PC '%s'...\n", commandStr, targetPeer)
					execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 45*time.Second)
					res, err := n.ExecuteRemoteCommand(execCtx, targetPeer, remoteshell.ShellRequest{
						Command:   commandStr,
						ShellType: remoteshell.ShellAuto,
					})
					cancelExec()

					if err != nil {
						fmt.Printf("[EXEC] Remote execution failed: %v\n", err)
						break
					}

					fmt.Println("=================================================================")
					fmt.Printf(" Remote Node: %s | Exit Code: %d | Duration: %d ms\n", targetPeer, res.ExitCode, res.DurationMs)
					if res.Error != "" {
						fmt.Printf(" [!] Error: %s\n", res.Error)
					}
					if res.Stdout != "" {
						fmt.Println(" --- STDOUT ---")
						fmt.Print(res.Stdout)
						if !strings.HasSuffix(res.Stdout, "\n") {
							fmt.Println()
						}
					}
					if res.Stderr != "" {
						fmt.Println(" --- STDERR ---")
						fmt.Print(res.Stderr)
						if !strings.HasSuffix(res.Stderr, "\n") {
							fmt.Println()
						}
					}
					fmt.Println("=================================================================")
				}
			case "run":
				if len(parts) < 4 || len(parts) > 5 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: run <peerID> <c|cpp|python> <source-file> [stdin-file]")
					fmt.Println(`Example: run node-b python "./hello world.py"`)
					break
				}
				peerID := parts[1]
				language := strings.ToLower(parts[2])
				if language != "c" && language != "cpp" && language != "python" {
					fmt.Println("Supported languages: c, cpp, python")
					break
				}
				fileInfo, statErr := os.Stat(parts[3])
				if statErr != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Cannot access source file: %v\n", statErr)
					break
				}
				if !fileInfo.Mode().IsRegular() || fileInfo.Size() > int64(codeexec.MaxSourceBytes) {
					fmt.Printf("Source file must be a regular file no larger than %d bytes.\n", codeexec.MaxSourceBytes)
					break
				}
				sourceBytes, readErr := os.ReadFile(parts[3])
				if readErr != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Cannot read source file: %v\n", readErr)
					break
				}
				stdin := ""
				if len(parts) == 5 {
					inputInfo, inputStatErr := os.Stat(parts[4])
					if inputStatErr != nil {
						fmt.Printf("Cannot access stdin file: %v\n", inputStatErr)
						break
					}
					if !inputInfo.Mode().IsRegular() || inputInfo.Size() > int64(codeexec.MaxStdinBytes) {
						fmt.Printf("Stdin file must be a regular file no larger than %d bytes.\n", codeexec.MaxStdinBytes)
						break
					}
					inputBytes, inputReadErr := os.ReadFile(parts[4])
					if inputReadErr != nil {
						fmt.Printf("Cannot read stdin file: %v\n", inputReadErr)
						break
					}
					stdin = string(inputBytes)
				}
				req := codeexec.Request{
					JobID: "job-" + uuid.New().String(), Language: language,
					Source: string(sourceBytes), Stdin: stdin, TimeoutSeconds: *codeTimeout,
				}
				fmt.Printf("[RUN] Submitting %s job %s to %s...\n", language, req.JobID, peerID)
				jobStart := time.Now()
				execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Duration(*codeTimeout+8)*time.Second)
				resp, execErr := n.ExecuteRemoteCode(execCtx, peerID, req)
				cancelExec()
				if execErr != nil {
					fmt.Printf("[RUN] Job failed: %v\n", execErr)
					break
				}
				fmt.Println("=================================================================")
				fmt.Printf(" Job ID: %s | Worker: %s | Language: %s\n", resp.JobID, peerID, resp.Language)
				if resp.TimedOut {
					fmt.Println(" Status: Timed out")
				} else if resp.ExitCode == 0 && resp.Error == "" {
					fmt.Println(" Status: Completed")
				} else {
					fmt.Println(" Status: Failed")
				}
				if resp.Error != "" { fmt.Printf(" Error: %s\n", resp.Error) }
				if resp.Stdout != "" {
					fmt.Println(" --- STDOUT ---")
					fmt.Print(resp.Stdout)
					if !strings.HasSuffix(resp.Stdout, "\n") { fmt.Println() }
				}
				if resp.Stderr != "" {
					fmt.Println(" --- STDERR ---")
					fmt.Print(resp.Stderr)
					if !strings.HasSuffix(resp.Stderr, "\n") { fmt.Println() }
				}
				if resp.OutputTruncated { fmt.Println(" [!] Output was truncated by the worker's output limit.") }
				fmt.Printf(" Exit code: %d | Worker execution: %d ms | Round trip: %d ms\n", resp.ExitCode, resp.DurationMs, time.Since(jobStart).Milliseconds())
				fmt.Println("=================================================================")
			case "gpu":
				prof, enabled := n.GPUProfile()
				if !enabled {
					fmt.Println("GPU subsystem is not enabled. Run node with -enable-gpu to activate Objective 3.")
					break
				}
				wdStatus, _ := n.GPUWatchdogStatus()
				fmt.Println("\n======================= Objective 3: GPU Hardware & Governance =======================")
				fmt.Printf(" Device Name:        %s\n", prof.DeviceName)
				fmt.Printf(" Vendor:             %s\n", prof.Vendor)
				fmt.Printf(" Total VRAM:         %d MB (%.2f GB)\n", prof.TotalVRAMBytes/(1024*1024), float64(prof.TotalVRAMBytes)/(1024*1024*1024))
				fmt.Printf(" Available VRAM:     %d MB\n", prof.AvailableVRAMBytes/(1024*1024))
				if prof.DriverVersion != "" {
					fmt.Printf(" Driver Version:     %s\n", prof.DriverVersion)
				}
				if prof.TemperatureC > 0 {
					fmt.Printf(" GPU Temperature:    %.1f °C | Power: %.1f W\n", prof.TemperatureC, prof.PowerUsageW)
				}
				fmt.Printf(" DirectML Support:   %v (Universal DirectX 12 acceleration across AMD/Intel/NVIDIA)\n", prof.DirectMLSupported)
				fmt.Printf(" CUDA Support:       %v\n", prof.CUDASupported)
				fmt.Printf(" Backends Detected:  %v\n", prof.SupportedBackends)
				fmt.Println("--------------------------------- 50 ms Watchdog State ---------------------------------")
				fmt.Printf(" Watchdog Status:    %s\n", wdStatus.State)
				fmt.Printf(" Power Source:       OnBattery=%v (%d%% remaining)\n", wdStatus.OnBattery, wdStatus.BatteryPercent)
				fmt.Printf(" User Activity:      Active=%v (Idle: %v | Sustained Idle: %v)\n",
					wdStatus.UserActive, wdStatus.UserIdleDuration.Round(time.Millisecond), wdStatus.SustainedIdlePeriod.Round(time.Second))
				if wdStatus.LastPauseReason != "" {
					fmt.Printf(" Last Pause Reason:  %s (%v ago)\n", wdStatus.LastPauseReason, time.Since(wdStatus.LastPauseTime).Round(time.Second))
				}
				fmt.Println("=======================================================================================")
			case "hipify":
				if len(parts) < 2 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: hipify <cuda-source-file>")
					fmt.Println("Example: hipify ./samples/cuda/vector_add.cu")
					break
				}
				cudaBytes, err := os.ReadFile(parts[1])
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Cannot read source file: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				res := gpu.TranslateCUDAToHIP(string(cudaBytes))
				fmt.Println("\n======================= CUDA -> AMD HIPIFY Portability Analysis =======================")
				fmt.Printf(" Source File:        %s (%d lines)\n", parts[1], res.Report.TotalLines)
				fmt.Printf(" Portable to AMD:    %v\n", res.Report.TargetAMDSupported)
				fmt.Printf(" Suggested Action:   %s\n", res.Report.SuggestedAction)
				if len(res.Report.Issues) > 0 {
					fmt.Printf("\n Detected %d Incompatibility Issue(s):\n", len(res.Report.Issues))
					for idx, iss := range res.Report.Issues {
						fmt.Printf("  [%d] Line %d: [%s] %s\n      Reason: %s\n      Remedy: %s\n",
							idx+1, iss.LineNumber, iss.Severity, iss.Construct, iss.Reason, iss.Remediation)
					}
				}
				if res.Success {
					fmt.Printf("\n[SUCCESS] Kernel successfully translated to portable HIP C++ (%d replacements made).\n", res.ReplacementsMade)
					fmt.Println("--- Translated Code Preview ---")
					lines := strings.Split(res.TranslatedSource, "\n")
					limit := 15
					if len(lines) < limit {
						limit = len(lines)
					}
					for i := 0; i < limit; i++ {
						fmt.Println(lines[i])
					}
					if len(lines) > limit {
						fmt.Printf("... (%d lines total)\n", len(lines))
					}
				} else {
					fmt.Printf("\n[BLOCKED] %s\n", res.Error)
				}
				fmt.Println("=======================================================================================")
			case "gpu-run":
				if len(parts) < 3 {
					fmt.Println("Usage: gpu-run <c|cpp|onnx> <source-file> [batches]")
					fmt.Println("Example: gpu-run onnx ./model.onnx 100")
					fmt.Println("Example: gpu-run cpp ./kernel.cu")
					break
				}
				lang := strings.ToLower(parts[1])
				filePath := parts[2]
				totalBatches := 50
				if len(parts) >= 4 {
					fmt.Sscanf(parts[3], "%d", &totalBatches)
				}
				srcBytes, err := os.ReadFile(filePath)
				if err != nil {
					fmt.Printf("Cannot read source file: %v\n", err)
					break
				}
				req := gpu.GPUTaskRequest{
					JobID: "gpu-job-" + uuid.New().String()[:8],
					Manifest: gpu.TaskCapsuleManifest{
						Name:         filepath.Base(filePath),
						TargetTier:   "tier3",
						TaskType:     "training",
						TotalBatches: totalBatches,
					},
					SourceCode: string(srcBytes),
					TimeoutSeconds: 60,
				}
				if lang == "onnx" {
					req.Manifest.TaskType = "inference"
					req.InputTensors = map[string][]float32{
						"input": {1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0},
					}
				}
				fmt.Printf("[GPU-RUN] Executing %s task %s under Win32 JobObject governance...\n", lang, req.JobID)
				execCtx, cancelExec := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
				resp, execErr := n.ExecuteGPUTask(execCtx, req)
				cancelExec()
				if execErr != nil {
					fmt.Printf("[GPU-RUN] Execution failed: %v\n", execErr)
					break
				}
				fmt.Println("\n============================ Objective 3 GPU Task Result ============================")
				fmt.Printf(" Job ID:          %s\n", resp.JobID)
				fmt.Printf(" Status:          %s\n", resp.Status)
				fmt.Printf(" Execution Time:  %d ms\n", resp.ExecutionMs)
				if resp.PreemptedReason != "" {
					fmt.Printf(" Preempted By:    %s\n", resp.PreemptedReason)
					fmt.Printf(" Checkpoint Saved: %s\n", resp.CheckpointBlob)
				}
				if resp.DiagnosticMessage != "" {
					fmt.Printf(" Diagnostic:      %s\n", resp.DiagnosticMessage)
				}
				if resp.Error != "" {
					fmt.Printf(" Error:           %s\n", resp.Error)
				}
				if len(resp.OutputTensors) > 0 {
					fmt.Printf(" Outputs:         %+v\n", resp.OutputTensors)
				}
				fmt.Println("=====================================================================================")
			case "quit", "exit":
				fmt.Println("Exiting node...")
				os.Exit(0)
			default:
				fmt.Printf("Unknown command: %s. Type 'help' for command list.\n", cmd)
			}
			fmt.Print("> ")
		}
	}()

	sigCh := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(sigCh, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	<-sigCh

	log.Println("[INFO] Shutting down UniCompute node gracefully...")
}

func handleGetBlob(n *node.Node, blobID string, destFile string) {
	rc, err := n.GetBlob(blobID)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("Error getting blob: %v\n", err)
		return
	}
	defer rc.Close()

	if destFile != "" {
		outFile, err := os.Create(destFile)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("Error creating output file: %v\n", err)
			return
		}
		defer outFile.Close()
		written, err := io.Copy(outFile, rc)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("Error saving blob: %v\n", err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("Exported blob %s (%d bytes) to %s\n", blobID, written, destFile)
		}
	} else {
		data, err := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(rc, 256))
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("Read error: %v\n", err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("Blob %s Preview: %s\n", blobID, string(data))
		}
	}
}

package main

import (
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"
	"time"

	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/relay"
)

func main() {
	listenAddr := flag.String("listen", "0.0.0.0:22067", "Contributor relay listen address")
	timeoutSec := flag.Int("timeout", 30, "Session timeout in seconds")

	flag.Parse()

	fmt.Println("===================================================================")
	fmt.Println(" UniCompute Contributor Relay (Syncthing Relay-v1 Model)")
	fmt.Printf(" Listening on: %s\n", *listenAddr)
	fmt.Println(" [DEPRECATED] Contributor relay is deprecated; use embedded/external TURN for WebRTC NAT traversal.")
	fmt.Println(" Opaque byte forwarding with blind end-to-end encryption")
	fmt.Println("===================================================================")

	r, err := relay.NewContributorRelay(relay.ServerConfig{
		ListenAddr:     *listenAddr,
		SessionTimeout: time.Duration(*timeoutSec) * time.Second,
	})
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatalf("[FATAL] Failed to start contributor relay: %v\n", err)
	}
	defer r.Close()

	log.Printf("[INFO] Contributor relay active on %s\n", r.Addr().String())

	sigCh := make(chan os.Signal, 1)
	signal.Notify(sigCh, os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	<-sigCh

	log.Printf("[INFO] Total bytes relayed: %d\n", r.TotalRelayedBytes())
	log.Println("[INFO] Shutting down contributor relay...")
}

FILE: cmd/verify-obj3/main.go

package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu/hipify"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu/onnx"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu/sandbox"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/gpu/watchdog"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println("================================================================================")
	fmt.Println(" UniCompute Objective 3: Cross-Platform GPU & Resource Governance Verification")
	fmt.Println("================================================================================")

	allPassed := true

	// 1. Hardware Probing Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 1] Probing Local Graphics Hardware (DXGI / NVML / DirectML / CUDA)...")
	ctxProbe, cancelProbe := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	profile, err := gpu.ProbeHardware(ctxProbe)
	cancelProbe()
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf(" [!] Hardware probe returned error: %v\n", err)
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Device:           %s\n", profile.DeviceName)
		fmt.Printf("  -> Vendor:           %s\n", profile.Vendor)
		fmt.Printf("  -> Total VRAM:       %d MB (%.2f GB)\n", profile.TotalVRAMBytes/(1024*1024), float64(profile.TotalVRAMBytes)/(1024*1024*1024))
		fmt.Printf("  -> Available VRAM:   %d MB\n", profile.AvailableVRAMBytes/(1024*1024))
		fmt.Printf("  -> DirectML Support: %v (DirectX 12 feature level verified)\n", profile.DirectMLSupported)
		fmt.Printf("  -> CUDA Support:     %v\n", profile.CUDASupported)
		fmt.Printf("  -> Backends:         %v\n", profile.SupportedBackends)
		fmt.Println("  [PASS] Hardware probe completed successfully.")
	}

	// 2. HIPIFY Portability & Warp-Check Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 2] Testing CUDA-to-AMD HIPIFY Analysis & Warp Verification...")
	portableFile := "samples/gpu/portable_vector_add.cu"
	warpFile := "samples/gpu/warp_reduction.cu"
	ptxFile := "samples/gpu/inline_ptx.cu"

	// 2a. Portable Kernel
	portableSrc, _ := os.ReadFile(portableFile)
	resPortable := hipify.TranslateCUDAToHIP(string(portableSrc))
	if !resPortable.Success || !resPortable.Report.TargetAMDSupported {
		fmt.Println("  [FAIL] Expected portable vectorAdd to pass AMD analysis.")
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Portable kernel: %d lines, %d replacements (cudaMalloc -> hipMalloc verified)\n",
			resPortable.Report.TotalLines, resPortable.ReplacementsMade)
		fmt.Println("  [PASS] Portable kernel translated to HIP successfully.")
	}

	// 2b. Warp Intrinsics Blocker
	warpSrc, _ := os.ReadFile(warpFile)
	resWarp := hipify.TranslateCUDAToHIP(string(warpSrc))
	if resWarp.Success || resWarp.Report.TargetAMDSupported {
		fmt.Println("  [FAIL] Expected warp reduction with __shfl_down_sync to be rejected for AMD.")
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Warp blocker caught: %d issue(s) detected. Action=%s\n",
			len(resWarp.Report.Issues), resWarp.Report.SuggestedAction)
		for _, iss := range resWarp.Report.Issues {
			fmt.Printf("     * Line %d: [%s] %s\n", iss.LineNumber, iss.Construct, iss.Reason)
		}
		fmt.Println("  [PASS] Warp reduction correctly blocked with diagnostic notification.")
	}

	// 2c. Inline PTX Blocker
	ptxSrc, _ := os.ReadFile(ptxFile)
	resPTX := hipify.TranslateCUDAToHIP(string(ptxSrc))
	if resPTX.Success || resPTX.Report.TargetAMDSupported {
		fmt.Println("  [FAIL] Expected inline PTX to be rejected for AMD.")
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Inline PTX caught: %d issue(s) detected. Action=%s\n",
			len(resPTX.Report.Issues), resPTX.Report.SuggestedAction)
		fmt.Println("  [PASS] Inline PTX correctly blocked from execution on AMD.")
	}

	// 3. Win32 JobObject Sandbox Governance Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 3] Testing Win32 JobObject Sandboxing & Memory Governance...")
	sb, err := sandbox.NewJobObjectSandbox(sandbox.SandboxConfig{
		MaxMemoryBytes: 512 * 1024 * 1024, // 512 MB ceiling
		MaxProcesses:   2,
		IdlePriority:   true,
		KillOnClose:    false, // Do not kill current test process on close
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] JobObject creation failed: %v\n", err)
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		// Assign current process to sandbox to verify Win32 JobObject API bindings
		pid := os.Getpid()
		if err := sb.AssignProcess(pid); err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("  [NOTE] AssignProcess note (process may already be in root job): %v\n", err)
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("  -> Successfully assigned PID %d into Win32 JobObject with IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS\n", pid)
		}
		_ = sb.Close()
		fmt.Println("  [PASS] Win32 JobObject sandbox limits configured and verified.")
	}

	// 4. Low-Latency 50 ms Watchdog Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 4] Testing 50 ms Background Watchdog (Battery & Activity Polling)...")
	var pauseRecorded bool
	var pauseReason string
	wd := watchdog.NewWatchdog(watchdog.Config{
		PollInterval:        50 * time.Millisecond,
		UserActiveThreshold: 1000 * time.Millisecond,
		ResumeGracePeriod:   5 * time.Second,
	}, func(reason string) {
		pauseRecorded = true
		pauseReason = reason
	}, nil)

	wd.Start()
	time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond) // Allow ticker to poll hardware
	wdStat := wd.Status()
	wd.Stop()

	fmt.Printf("  -> Watchdog State:       %s\n", wdStat.State)
	fmt.Printf("  -> Power Status:        OnBattery=%v (%d%% remaining)\n", wdStat.OnBattery, wdStat.BatteryPercent)
	fmt.Printf("  -> User Input Status:   Active=%v (Idle time: %v)\n", wdStat.UserActive, wdStat.UserIdleDuration)
	if pauseRecorded {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Immediate Pause:     Triggered with reason: %q\n", pauseReason)
	}
	fmt.Println("  [PASS] 50 ms Watchdog polled system power and input telemetry accurately.")

	// 5. ONNX Checkpoint Integrity & Serialization Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 5] Testing ONNX Checkpoint Integrity & SHA-256 Verification...")
	tmpDir, _ := os.MkdirTemp("", "obj3-verify-*")
	defer os.RemoveAll(tmpDir)

	ckptFile := filepath.Join(tmpDir, "checkpoint.ckpt")
	originalCkpt := onnx.Checkpoint{
		JobID:     "job-verify-1",
		ModelHash: "model-convnet-v2",
		Step:      42,
		Epoch:     1,
		Loss:      0.31415,
		Weights: map[string][]float32{
			"layer.weight": {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4},
		},
	}
	hash, err := onnx.SaveCheckpoint(originalCkpt, ckptFile)
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] SaveCheckpoint failed: %v\n", err)
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		loadedCkpt, err := onnx.LoadCheckpoint(ckptFile)
		if err != nil || loadedCkpt.Step != 42 {
			fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] LoadCheckpoint failed: %v\n", err)
			allPassed = false
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("  -> Checkpoint SHA-256:  %s\n", hash)
			fmt.Println("  [PASS] Checkpoint atomically persisted, loaded, and verified.")
		}
	}

	// 6. Interruptible Training Loop & Preemption Migration Verification
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 6] Testing Interruptible Training Loop & Preemption Resumption [SIMULATED / MOCK ONNX RUNNER]...")
	engine := onnx.NewSessionEngine(onnx.ModelConfig{BatchSize: 8}, originalCkpt)
	migrationCkpt := filepath.Join(tmpDir, "migrated_checkpoint.ckpt")

	// Trigger watchdog preemption after 15 ms
	go func() {
		time.Sleep(15 * time.Millisecond)
		engine.TriggerPreempt("Student started 3D game (GPU load detected)")
	}()

	trainRes, _ := engine.RunTrainingLoop(context.Background(), 200, 5, migrationCkpt)
	if !trainRes.Preempted {
		fmt.Println("  [FAIL] Expected training to be preempted by watchdog.")
		allPassed = false
	} else if !trainRes.Simulated {
		fmt.Println("  [FAIL] Expected trainRes.Simulated to be true for educational mock runner.")
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		fmt.Printf("  -> Preempted at Step:   %d with reason: %q (Simulated: %v)\n", trainRes.TotalSteps, trainRes.PreemptReason, trainRes.Simulated)
		fmt.Printf("  -> Checkpoint Flushed:  %s (SHA-256: %s)\n", trainRes.CheckpointPath, trainRes.CheckpointHash)

		// Resume on second node engine
		resumedCkpt, err := onnx.LoadCheckpoint(migrationCkpt)
		if err != nil {
			fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] Failed to reload flushed checkpoint: %v\n", err)
			allPassed = false
		} else {
			secondEngine := onnx.NewSessionEngine(onnx.ModelConfig{BatchSize: 8}, resumedCkpt)
			secondRes, err := secondEngine.RunTrainingLoop(context.Background(), 10, 5, migrationCkpt)
			if err != nil || secondRes.TotalSteps <= resumedCkpt.Step {
				fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] Resumption failed: %v\n", err)
				allPassed = false
			} else {
				fmt.Printf("  -> Resumed on Peer:     Advanced from step %d to step %d\n", resumedCkpt.Step, secondRes.TotalSteps)
				fmt.Println("  [PASS] Training successfully paused, flushed to storage, and resumed.")
			}
		}
	}

	// 7. Full GPUManager Unified Orchestration Test
	fmt.Println("\n[TEST 7] Testing Unified GPUManager Orchestration [SIMULATED / MOCK ONNX RUNNER]...")
	mgr, err := gpu.NewManager(gpu.ManagerConfig{
		StorageDir:       tmpDir,
		MaxMemoryBytes:   512 * 1024 * 1024,
		WatchdogInterval: 50 * time.Millisecond,
		IgnoreBattery:    true,
	})
	if err != nil {
		fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] NewManager failed: %v\n", err)
		allPassed = false
	} else {
		mgr.Start()
		time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)
		taskReq := gpu.GPUTaskRequest{
			JobID: "job-unified-test",
			Manifest: gpu.TaskCapsuleManifest{
				Name:         "test-capsule",
				TargetTier:   "tier3",
				TaskType:     "training",
				TotalBatches: 20,
			},
		}
		taskResp := mgr.ExecuteTask(context.Background(), taskReq)
		_ = mgr.Close()
		if taskResp.Status != "completed" && taskResp.Status != "preempted" {
			fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] Task execution status: %s, error: %s\n", taskResp.Status, taskResp.Error)
			allPassed = false
		} else if !taskResp.Simulated {
			fmt.Printf("  [FAIL] Expected taskResp.Simulated to be true, got %v\n", taskResp.Simulated)
			allPassed = false
		} else {
			fmt.Printf("  -> Task ID:             %s (Status: %s, Time: %d ms, Batches: %d, Simulated: %v)\n",
				taskResp.JobID, taskResp.Status, taskResp.ExecutionMs, taskResp.ProcessedBatches, taskResp.Simulated)
			fmt.Println("  [PASS] Unified GPUManager orchestrated execution successfully.")
		}
	}

	fmt.Println("\n================================================================================")
	if allPassed {
		fmt.Println(" [SUCCESS] ALL OBJECTIVE 3 TESTS PASSED! Cross-Platform GPU Engine Operational.")
	} else {
		fmt.Println(" [FAILURE] One or more Objective 3 tests failed.")
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	fmt.Println("================================================================================")
}

# Caddyfile: Automated Let's Encrypt TLS (WSS port 443) for UniCompute Coordinator
# Replace {$COORDINATOR_DOMAIN:coordinator.unicompute.edu} with your public domain name or VM IP

{$COORDINATOR_DOMAIN:coordinator.unicompute.edu} {
    # WebSocket Signaling Proxy (WSS)
    handle /ws* {
        reverse_proxy coordinator:8080
    }

    # Health Check Endpoint
    handle /health* {
        reverse_proxy coordinator:8080
    }

    # Fleet Node Telemetry API
    handle /api/* {
        reverse_proxy coordinator:8080
    }

    # Fallback to coordinator
    handle {
        reverse_proxy coordinator:8080
    }

    # Security Headers
    header {
        Strict-Transport-Security "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
        X-Content-Type-Options "nosniff"
        X-Frame-Options "DENY"
    }

    log {
        output stdout
        format console
    }
}

# Multi-stage Dockerfile for UniCompute Cloud Coordinator
FROM golang:1.22-alpine AS builder

WORKDIR /app

# Install build dependencies
RUN apk add --no-cache git ca-certificates

# Cache dependencies
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN go mod download

# Copy source code
COPY . .

# Compile static binary for Linux
RUN CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64 go build -ldflags="-w -s" -o /unicompute-coordinator ./cmd/unicompute-coordinator

# Minimal runtime image
FROM alpine:3.19

RUN apk --no-cache add ca-certificates tzdata

WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=builder /unicompute-coordinator /app/unicompute-coordinator

# Create unprivileged application user
RUN adduser -D unicompute
USER unicompute

# Expose HTTP/WSS signaling port (8080) and TURN relay UDP port (3478)
EXPOSE 8080/tcp
EXPOSE 3478/udp

# Environment defaults
ENV UNICOMPUTE_LISTEN="0.0.0.0:8080" \
    UNICOMPUTE_REALM="unicompute.edu"

ENTRYPOINT ["/app/unicompute-coordinator"]

# UniCompute Cloud Coordinator Deployment Guide

This guide details how to deploy the **UniCompute Central Coordinator & Signaling Hub** to any cloud server (AWS EC2, Google Cloud Compute Engine, DigitalOcean, or a campus VM running Ubuntu Linux 22.04/24.04 LTS), matching the specification in Section 9 of the system architecture.

---

## 1. Network & Firewall Requirements

Open the following ports on your cloud provider security group / firewall:

| Port | Protocol | Purpose | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| **443** | TCP | Secure WebSocket Signaling (`wss://your-domain/ws`) & Web UI | Inbound |
| **80** | TCP | HTTP-01 Let's Encrypt automated TLS certificate issuance | Inbound |
| **3478** | UDP | STUN & Embedded TURN server (NAT Traversal Relay) | Inbound |
| **8080** | TCP | Direct WebSocket signaling (optional if using reverse proxy) | Inbound |

---

## 2. Option A: Docker Compose Deployment (Recommended)

Requires Docker and Docker Compose installed on your server.

### 1. Clone repository on the server
```bash
git clone https://github.com/your-org/UniComputeOBJ1.git
cd UniComputeOBJ1
```

### 2. Configure Environment
Create a `.env` file in `deploy/`:
```bash
cat <<EOF > deploy/.env
DOMAIN=coordinator.yourdomain.com
PUBLIC_IP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org)
REALM=unicompute.edu
TURN_SECRET=campus-volunteer-secret-2026
AUTH_TOKEN=<your-cluster-secret>
EOF
```

### 3. Start Services
```bash
cd deploy
docker compose up -d --build
```

### 4. Verify Deployment
```bash
# Check container status
docker compose ps

# Check Coordinator health endpoint
curl https://coordinator.yourdomain.com/health
# Response: {"status":"healthy","service":"unicompute-coordinator"}

# Check online fleet nodes
curl https://coordinator.yourdomain.com/api/nodes
# Response: {"count":0,"nodes":[]}
```

---

## 3. Option B: Native Ubuntu VM (Bare-Metal / Systemd)

Follow these steps if you are deploying directly to an Ubuntu 22.04 or 24.04 LTS VM without Docker.

### 1. Run the Auto-Provisioning Script
```bash
chmod +x deploy/setup-ubuntu.sh
./deploy/setup-ubuntu.sh
```

The script will automatically:
1. Configure UFW firewall rules (TCP 80, 443; UDP 3478).
2. Install Go 1.22+.
3. Compile `unicompute-coordinator` into `/opt/unicompute/`.
4. Install and start the `unicompute-coordinator.service` systemd daemon.

### 2. Inspect Service Status
```bash
sudo systemctl status unicompute-coordinator
```

### 3. View Live Logs
```bash
sudo journalctl -u unicompute-coordinator -f
```

---

## 4. Connecting Volunteer Laptops to Your Cloud Coordinator

Once your cloud coordinator is online, any student laptop in the world can connect simply by supplying the cloud coordinator's address:

### Secure TLS (with Domain & Caddy/Nginx)
```powershell
.\bin\unicompute-node.exe -id student-laptop-1 -signaling wss://coordinator.yourdomain.com/ws
```

### Direct IP (No Domain)
```powershell
.\bin\unicompute-node.exe -id student-laptop-1 -signaling ws://YOUR_SERVER_PUBLIC_IP:8080/ws
```

---

## 5. Invariant CP-1 Verification in Cloud
Once two nodes connect through your cloud coordinator:
1. Establish a WebRTC P2P connection between Node A and Node B.
2. Stop the coordinator service on the cloud server: `docker compose stop coordinator` (or `sudo systemctl stop unicompute-coordinator`).
3. Notice that chunk transfers, streaming, and data operations between Node A and Node B continue over their direct WebRTC SCTP DataChannel without interruption.

# Deploying the UniCompute Coordinator on Render

This guide outlines how to host the UniCompute Central Coordinator on [Render](https://render.com), along with key architectural considerations and limitations of PaaS platforms.

---

## 1. Architectural Considerations on Render

| Feature | Supported on Render? | Notes & Workaround |
|---|---|---|
| **WebSocket Signaling (WSS)** | **YES (Native)** | Render terminates TLS and provides free HTTPS/WSS on port 443 out of the box. |
| **Health Checks & APIs** | **YES** | Health endpoint at `/health` and node registry at `/api/nodes`. |
| **Direct Peer-to-Peer Data** | **YES (Unaffected)** | Data travels directly between laptops over UDP hole punching; never touches Render. |
| **Embedded UDP TURN Relay** | **NO** | Render Web Services only route HTTP/TCP. Raw UDP port 3478 is not exposed. Set `UNICOMPUTE_TURN=false`. |
| **Free Tier Spin-Down** | **Notice** | Free instances sleep after 15 min of inactivity. Keep warm using UptimeRobot / cron-job.org hitting `/health`. |

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Deployment Instructions

### Method A: Connect GitHub to Render Dashboard (Easiest)

1. Push your code to GitHub:
   ```bash
   git add .
   git commit -m "Add Render support"
   git push origin main
   ```

2. Go to the [Render Dashboard](https://dashboard.render.com/) and click **New +** $\to$ **Web Service**.
3. Select your GitHub repository.
4. Fill in the service settings:
   - **Name**: `unicompute-coordinator`
   - **Language / Runtime**: `Go`
   - **Build Command**: `go build -o unicompute-coordinator ./cmd/unicompute-coordinator`
   - **Start Command**: `./unicompute-coordinator`
   - **Plan**: `Free` (or `Starter`)
5. Under **Advanced** $\to$ **Health Check Path**, enter: `/health`
6. Under **Environment Variables**, add:
   - `UNICOMPUTE_TURN`: `false`
   - `UNICOMPUTE_REALM`: `unicompute.edu`
7. Click **Create Web Service**.

---

### Method B: Render Blueprint (`render.yaml`)

Because [`render.yaml`](file:///c:/Users/HP/Desktop/Noval/Projects/UniComputeOBJ1/render.yaml) is included in the root directory:
1. Go to [Render Dashboard](https://dashboard.render.com/) $\to$ **Blueprints**.
2. Select your repository.
3. Render will automatically detect `render.yaml` and configure the Web Service with health check and environment variables.
4. Click **Apply**.

---

## 3. Connecting Volunteer Laptops to Render

Once deployed, Render gives you a URL like:
`https://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com`

Volunteer student laptops can now connect from anywhere in the world using:

```powershell
.\bin\unicompute-node.exe -id student-laptop-1 -signaling wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws
```

---

## 4. NAT Traversal & Fallback Strategy with Render

Since Render cannot serve as a UDP TURN relay, how does UniCompute handle NAT traversal?

1. **Direct P2P (80–85% of connections)**:
   - The coordinator exchanges ICE candidates.
   - The laptops use Google's free public STUN (`stun.l.google.com:19302`) to discover their public UDP endpoints.
   - Dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 hole punching connects them directly.
2. **Strict Symmetric NAT / Firewall Fallback**:
   - If direct UDP hole punching fails between two firewalled laptops, use UniCompute's built-in **Contributor Relay** (`unicompute-relay` or student laptops running with `-run-relay`).
   - Alternatively, supply a free external TURN server (such as Metered.ca's 50GB free tier) in `node.NodeConfig`.

version: '3.8'

services:
  coordinator:
    build:
      context: ..
      dockerfile: deploy/Dockerfile
    restart: unless-stopped
    environment:
      - UNICOMPUTE_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8080
      - UNICOMPUTE_PUBLIC_IP=${PUBLIC_IP:-}
      - UNICOMPUTE_REALM=${REALM:-unicompute.edu}
      - UNICOMPUTE_TURN_SECRET=${TURN_SECRET:-}
      - UNICOMPUTE_AUTH_TOKEN=${AUTH_TOKEN:-}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"      # Internal / Direct WebSocket signaling
      - "3478:3478/udp"  # STUN / Embedded TURN UDP port
    networks:
      - unicompute-net

  caddy:
    image: caddy:2-alpine
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "80:80"    # HTTP (redirects to HTTPS / ACME challenges)
      - "443:443"  # HTTPS & WSS (Secure WebSocket Signaling)
    environment:
      - COORDINATOR_DOMAIN=${DOMAIN:-coordinator.unicompute.edu}
    volumes:
      - ./Caddyfile:/etc/caddy/Caddyfile:ro
      - caddy_data:/data
      - caddy_config:/config
    depends_on:
      - coordinator
    networks:
      - unicompute-net

networks:
  unicompute-net:
    driver: bridge

volumes:
  caddy_data:
  caddy_config:

FILE: deploy/setup-ubuntu.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ==============================================================================
# UniCompute Cloud Coordinator Auto-Provisioning Script (Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 LTS)
# Specifications matching Section 9 of the UniCompute System Architecture
# ==============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

echo "==================================================================="
echo " UniCompute Coordinator Installation & Setup"
echo "==================================================================="

# 1. Update OS packages
sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get upgrade -y
sudo apt-get install -y curl wget git build-essential ufw debian-keyring debian-archive-keyring apt-transport-https

# 2. Configure Firewall (UFW)
echo "[INFO] Configuring firewall rules..."
sudo ufw allow 22/tcp comment 'SSH'
sudo ufw allow 80/tcp comment 'HTTP (ACME)'
sudo ufw allow 443/tcp comment 'HTTPS / WSS Signaling'
sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp comment 'Coordinator Direct WS/HTTP'
sudo ufw allow 3478/udp comment 'STUN / Embedded TURN'
sudo ufw --force enable

# 3. Detect Public IP
PUBLIC_IP=$(curl -s https://api.ipify.org || curl -s https://ifconfig.me || echo "127.0.0.1")
echo "[INFO] Detected Public IP: ${PUBLIC_IP}"

# 4. Install Go 1.22+ if not installed
if ! command -v go &> /dev/null; then
    echo "[INFO] Installing Go 1.22.8..."
    wget -q https://go.dev/dl/go1.22.8.linux-amd64.tar.gz
    sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go && sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf go1.22.8.linux-amd64.tar.gz
    rm go1.22.8.linux-amd64.tar.gz
    echo 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin' >> ~/.profile
    export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin
fi

# 5. Create unicompute service user and directory
sudo useradd -r -s /bin/false -d /opt/unicompute unicompute || true
sudo mkdir -p /opt/unicompute
sudo chown -R unicompute:unicompute /opt/unicompute

# 6. Build coordinator binary
echo "[INFO] Compiling unicompute-coordinator..."
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -o /tmp/unicompute-coordinator ./cmd/unicompute-coordinator
sudo mv /tmp/unicompute-coordinator /opt/unicompute/unicompute-coordinator
sudo chmod +x /opt/unicompute/unicompute-coordinator
sudo chown unicompute:unicompute /opt/unicompute/unicompute-coordinator

# 7. Install Environment Config
sudo bash -c "cat <<EOF > /etc/default/unicompute-coordinator
PUBLIC_IP=${PUBLIC_IP}
UNICOMPUTE_LISTEN=0.0.0.0:8080
UNICOMPUTE_PUBLIC_IP=${PUBLIC_IP}
UNICOMPUTE_REALM=unicompute.edu
EOF"

# 8. Install Systemd Service
sudo cp deploy/unicompute-coordinator.service /etc/systemd/system/
sudo systemctl daemon-reload
sudo systemctl enable unicompute-coordinator
sudo systemctl restart unicompute-coordinator

echo "[INFO] Service status:"
sudo systemctl status unicompute-coordinator --no-pager

echo ""
echo "==================================================================="
echo " Coordinator successfully deployed and running!"
echo " Public IP:     ${PUBLIC_IP}"
echo " Signaling URL: ws://${PUBLIC_IP}:8080/ws"
echo " Health Check:  http://${PUBLIC_IP}:8080/health"
echo "==================================================================="

================================================
FILE: deploy/unicompute-coordinator.service
================================================
[Unit]
Description=UniCompute Central Coordinator & Signaling Hub
After=network.target
Wants=network-online.target

[Service]
Type=simple
User=unicompute
Group=unicompute
WorkingDirectory=/opt/unicompute
ExecStart=/opt/unicompute/unicompute-coordinator \
    -listen 0.0.0.0:8080 \
    -public-ip ${PUBLIC_IP} \
    -realm unicompute.edu \
    -turn=true \
    -turn-port 3478
Restart=always
RestartSec=5s
LimitNOFILE=65536

# Security hardening
NoNewPrivileges=true
ProtectSystem=full
ProtectHome=true

EnvironmentFile=-/etc/default/unicompute-coordinator

[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target

# UniCompute: Objectives 1, 2, 3 & Desktop GUI — Linux Deployment, Operation & Testing Guide

This guide provides end-to-end instructions for installing prerequisites, compiling static CGO-free binaries, configuring firewalls, operating, and verifying the **UniCompute Volunteer Compute & Distributed Storage Fleet (Objectives 1, 2, and 3)** alongside the **Interactive Desktop GUI Control Room** across major Linux distributions (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04 LTS, Debian 12, Fedora 40/41, and Arch Linux).

## 1. Architecture Overview & Binaries

UniCompute integrates distributed volunteer compute, storage, and cross-platform hardware acceleration across three primary objectives:
- **Objective 1 (P2P Transport & Storage Substrate)**: Dual-stack ICE, CGNAT RFC 6598 hole punching, blind contributor relay fallback, WebRTC SCTP multiplexing (`dc-ctrl` and `dc-bulk`), and content-addressed storage (CAS) disk vault with SHA-256 scrub auditing.
- **Objective 2 (Isolated Compute Engine)**: Air-gapped Docker container execution (`--network none`, `--memory 128m`, `--cpus 1.0`, `--read-only`, dropping all capabilities), remote shell execution, and language runtimes (C/C++, Python).
- **Objective 3 (Cross-Platform GPU Acceleration & Governance)**: Hardware probing (CUDA, ROCm, Vulkan), 50 ms battery/activity watchdog preemption, cgroup/setrlimit memory limits, CUDA-to-AMD HIPIFY analysis & translation, and ONNX training checkpoint persistence.
- **Desktop GUI Control Room**: A standalone desktop app featuring a 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas topology engine (central mainframe tower, orbiting dual-hemisphere workstation rigs, glowing P2P laser beams) and 4 dedicated control panels.

The project compiles into standalone, CGO-free Linux ELF executables in the `bin/` directory:

| Binary | Description |
|---|---|
| `bin/unicompute-gui` | **Desktop GUI Control Room**. Static CGO-free ELF executable with embedded 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas topology engine, hardware dials, and multi-objective tabs. Protected with cryptographic session token auth and strict loopback Origin checks. Compatible with Ubuntu 18/20/22/24 LTS. |
| `bin/unicompute-node` | **Contributor Peer Node Daemon & CLI**. Manages local CAS vault, WebRTC SCTP connections, Docker sandbox execution, remote shell (opt-in + allowlist), and GPU acceleration. |
| `bin/unicompute-coordinator` | **Signaling Hub & Embedded TURN Server**. Relays WebSocket SDP offers/answers, ICE candidates, and fleet registry. Protected via cluster auth tokens (`-auth-token`) and duplicate node ID hijacking rejection. |
| `bin/unicompute-relay` | **Contributor Relay Daemon (Deprecated)**. Legacy byte relay fallback; modern deployments rely on native Pion ICE and embedded/external TURN. |
| `bin/verify-obj3` | **Objective 3 Automated Hardware Verification Suite**. 7-point validation suite for physical GPU, watchdog, sandboxing, and simulated ONNX execution. |

**Live Production Coordinator**: A central signaling coordinator is live on Render at:
`wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws`

**Linux GUI Launcher**:
- Execute `./run-gui.sh` to start the daemon and launch the desktop window.
- Build static binaries using `./build_linux.sh`.

---

## 2. Prerequisites Installation across Linux Distributions

Ensure your Linux system has:
- 64-bit x86_64 or ARM64 architecture.
- Kernel 5.15+ (with cgroup v2 enabled, default on modern distros).
- At least 4 GB RAM and 15 GB available disk space.

### 2.1 Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04 LTS & Debian 12

Update the package cache and install essential build tools:
```bash
sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade -y
sudo apt install -y git curl build-essential ca-certificates gnupg lsb-release
```

#### Install Go 1.22+ / 1.23+
Download and extract the official Go binary release:
```bash
GO_VERSION="1.22.8"
curl -OL "https://go.dev/dl/go${GO_VERSION}.linux-amd64.tar.gz"
sudo rm -rf /usr/local/go
sudo tar -C /usr/local -xzf "go${GO_VERSION}.linux-amd64.tar.gz"
rm "go${GO_VERSION}.linux-amd64.tar.gz"

# Add Go to PATH in ~/.bashrc
if ! grep -q "/usr/local/go/bin" ~/.bashrc; then
    echo 'export PATH=$PATH:/usr/local/go/bin' >> ~/.bashrc
fi
source ~/.bashrc
```

Verify Go:
```bash
go version
# Expected: go version go1.22+ linux/amd64
```

#### Install Docker Engine
```bash
sudo apt install -y docker.io docker-compose-plugin
```

---

### 2.2 Fedora 40 / 41 & RHEL 9

Install build tools and Go:
```bash
sudo dnf install -y git curl gcc gcc-c++ make golang
```

Install Docker:
```bash
sudo dnf install -y moby-engine docker-compose-plugin
```

---

### 2.3 Arch Linux

```bash
sudo pacman -Syu --noconfirm git curl base-devel go docker
```

---

### 2.4 Docker User Group & Service Activation

To allow running Docker containers without `sudo` (required by `unicompute-node` when running code execution jobs):

```bash
# Enable and start Docker service
sudo systemctl enable --now docker

# Add your user to the docker group
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER

# Apply the new group membership to the current shell
newgrp docker
```

Verify that Docker works without `sudo`:
```bash
docker run --rm hello-world
```
If you see `"Hello from Docker!"`, your Docker environment is properly configured.

---

### 2.5 GPU Acceleration Drivers & Libraries (CUDA / ROCm)

For Objective 3 GPU acceleration and telemetry on Linux:
- **NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)**:
  - Install the NVIDIA proprietary driver (`nvidia-driver-535` or `nvidia-driver-550`):
    ```bash
    sudo apt install -y nvidia-driver-550
    ```
  - Verify CUDA driver detection:
    ```bash
    nvidia-smi
    ```
- **AMD Radeon (ROCm / HIP)**:
  - On Ubuntu 22.04 / 24.04, install ROCm packages (`rocm-hip-sdk` or `hip-runtime-amd`):
    ```bash
    sudo apt install -y hip-runtime-amd
    ```
- **Linux GPU Monitoring Permissions**:
  - Ensure the user belongs to the `video` and `render` groups to access GPU device nodes (`/dev/kfd`, `/dev/dri/*`):
    ```bash
    sudo usermod -aG video,render $USER
    ```

---

### 2.6 Desktop GUI Browser Runtime (Chromium / Chrome / Edge)

The Desktop GUI Control Room runs as a native application window. Install Chromium or Google Chrome:
- **Ubuntu / Debian**:
  ```bash
  sudo apt install -y chromium-browser || sudo apt install -y chromium
  ```
- **Fedora**:
  ```bash
  sudo dnf install -y chromium
  ```
- **Arch Linux**:
  ```bash
  sudo pacman -S --noconfirm chromium
  ```
When running `./run-gui.sh`, the launcher automatically probes `google-chrome`, `chromium-browser`, `chromium`, `microsoft-edge`, and falls back to `xdg-open` if no standalone browser is found.

---

## 3. Linux Firewall & Network Setup for WebRTC

UniCompute utilizes dual-stack STUN probing (`stun.l.google.com:19302`) and WebRTC ICE hole punching over dynamic UDP ports. On consumer broadband and cloud VPS instances, stateful firewalls require specific rules.

### 3.1 UFW (Ubuntu / Debian)

If UFW is active:
```bash
# Allow outgoing UDP for STUN and WebRTC hole punching (usually allowed by default)
sudo ufw default allow outgoing

# If hosting a local coordinator:
sudo ufw allow 8080/tcp comment "UniCompute Coordinator WebSocket"

# If hosting a contributor relay:
sudo ufw allow 22067/tcp comment "UniCompute Contributor Relay"

# If running an embedded TURN server:
sudo ufw allow 3478/udp comment "UniCompute TURN Relay"

sudo ufw reload
sudo ufw status verbose
```

### 3.2 firewalld (Fedora / RHEL)

```bash
# If hosting coordinator / relay / TURN services:
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=8080/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=22067/tcp
sudo firewall-cmd --permanent --add-port=3478/udp
sudo firewall-cmd --reload
```

### 3.3 Kernel UDP & Docker Forwarding Notes

1. **Docker Bridge Forwarding**: Ensure the Linux kernel allows packet forwarding across Docker bridges:
   ```bash
   sudo sysctl -w net.ipv4.ip_forward=1
   sudo iptables -P FORWARD ACCEPT
   ```
2. **Virtual Adapter Pruning**: UniCompute's built-in `pkg/nat` module automatically prunes virtual interfaces (`docker0`, `br-*`, `veth*`, `tailscale0`, `tun*`, `tap*`) so they do not pollute WebRTC candidate harvesting with unroutable private addresses.

---

## 4. Cloning the Repository & Go Version Alignment

### 4.1 Git Clone
```bash
git clone https://github.com/unicompute/obj1.git UniComputeOBJ1
cd UniComputeOBJ1
```

### 4.2 Handling `go.mod` Version Alignment (`go 1.22`)
If your Linux system has Go 1.22 installed and the `go.mod` file references a newer toolchain version, align the module with a single command:

```bash
go mod edit -go 1.22
go mod tidy
```
This ensures zero compilation errors and avoids automatic toolchain download attempts.

## 5. Compiling Static CGO-Free Binaries (`build_linux.sh`)

Compile all UniCompute binaries as static, portable ELF executables with stripped debugging symbols (`-ldflags="-s -w"`) and `CGO_ENABLED=0`. This ensures 100% portability across modern Linux distributions (Ubuntu 22.04/24.04, Debian 12, Fedora) as well as legacy systems (Ubuntu 18.04/20.04) with zero glibc shared library dependencies:

```bash
# Automated compilation:
chmod +x build_linux.sh
./build_linux.sh
```

Or compile manually:
```bash
mkdir -p bin

# 1. Compile Node daemon & CLI
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o bin/unicompute-node ./cmd/unicompute-node

# 2. Compile Central Signaling Coordinator
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o bin/unicompute-coordinator ./cmd/unicompute-coordinator

# 3. Compile Contributor Relay
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o bin/unicompute-relay ./cmd/unicompute-relay

# 4. Compile Desktop GUI Control Room (Linux Static ELF)
CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags="-s -w" -o bin/unicompute-gui ./cmd/unicompute-gui

# Ensure executables have execution permissions
chmod +x bin/*
```

Verify the compiled binaries:
```bash
ls -lh bin/
file bin/unicompute-gui
# Expected: ELF 64-bit LSB executable, x86-64 (or aarch64), statically linked, stripped
```

## 6. Running the Automated Verification Suite

Run the full automated verification suite to validate all 12 Go packages, Objective 3 GPU hardware probes, and standalone samples:

```bash
# 1. Run all package unit tests:
go test -v ./pkg/blobstore ./pkg/codeexec ./pkg/gpu ./pkg/gpu/hipify ./pkg/gpu/onnx ./pkg/instrumentation ./pkg/nat ./pkg/node ./pkg/relay ./pkg/remoteshell ./pkg/signaling ./pkg/transport

# 2. Run standalone samples verification runner:
go run ./cmd/test-samples

# 3. Run Objective 3 physical hardware & governance suite:
go run ./cmd/verify-obj3
```

*(Note: On systems with PowerShell Core installed (`pwsh`), you can run `pwsh -File ./test_all.ps1` for the full 30-point scorecard).*

### Test Suite Coverage:
- **`pkg/blobstore`**: Atomic filesystem commits, SHA-256 verification, quota accounting, bitrot scrub audit.
- **`pkg/codeexec`**: Bounded code request/response framing, 12 KiB source and 4 KiB stdin ceiling checks.
- **`pkg/gpu`**: Hardware capability discovery, ROCm/CUDA dynamic loading, temperature/VRAM monitoring.
- **`pkg/gpu/hipify`**: Static AST analysis, 32-thread warp blocker detection, and CUDA-to-HIP AST translation.
- **`pkg/gpu/onnx`**: Model checkpoint serialization, SHA-256 state hashing, interruptible preemption loop.
- **`pkg/instrumentation`**: Prometheus metrics counters and histograms.
- **`pkg/nat`**: RFC 6598 CGNAT detection (`100.64.0.0/10`), dual-stack STUN probing, and virtual adapter pruning (`docker0`, `veth`).
- **`pkg/relay`**: Syncthing relay-v1 blind end-to-end byte transfer and embedded TURN server lifecycle.
- **`pkg/remoteshell`**: Linux shell execution (`/bin/sh`, `/bin/bash`) and timeout enforcement.
- **`pkg/signaling`**: WebSocket registration, 20-second keepalives, and candidate relay dispatch.
- **`pkg/transport`**: WebRTC PeerConnection, 16 MiB SCTP receive buffer, and dual DataChannels (`dc-ctrl` and `dc-bulk`).
- **`pkg/node`**: End-to-end chunk exchange and **Invariant CP-1 (Data Plane Independence)**.
- **`pkg/node`**: End-to-end chunk exchange and **Invariant CP-1 (Data Plane Independence)** verifying data transfer resilience if the coordinator fails.

## 8. Running a 2-Node Cluster on Linux

Open **two separate terminal tabs or windows**:
- **Terminal 1 (Worker Node B)**: Enables Docker sandbox code execution, contributes storage, and serves jobs from allowed peers.
- **Terminal 2 (Client Node A)**: Connects to Node B, transfers files into the CAS vault, issues shell commands, and submits jobs.

> [!NOTE]
> **Coordinator Architecture & Authentication**:
> - The Coordinator (`unicompute-coordinator` or the live Render cloud deployment) is a **headless signaling hub and embedded TURN server**. It intentionally has **no standalone web GUI**, ensuring zero footprint and maximum throughput on the signaling control plane.
> - **Cluster Authentication (`-auth-token`)**: When exposed on non-loopback addresses, the coordinator enforces cluster secret token authentication to prevent unauthorized signaling, node hijacking, and enumeration. Pass `-auth-token <secret>` or set `UNICOMPUTE_AUTH_TOKEN`. (For offline local testing without authentication, pass `-insecure-no-auth`).
> - **Verifying Coordinator Health via API**:
>   ```bash
>   # Health & Uptime Check (Live Render):
>   curl -s https://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/health
>   # Discovered Fleet Registry (add Bearer header if auth is enabled):
>   curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/api/nodes
>   # Local Coordinator:
>   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
>   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/nodes
>   ```
> - **Visualizing the Coordinator in the Desktop GUI**: The visual representation of the coordinator lives inside the **Desktop GUI Control Room** (`unicompute-gui`). When you launch the GUI, **Tab 1: P2P Topology Mesh** renders the coordinator as the central glowing mainframe tower, dynamically surrounded by orbiting worker rigs.

### Option A: Public Live Coordinator on Render

---

### 9.4 Air-Gapped Docker Sandbox Code Execution (`run`)

The `run` command reads a local source file on Client Node A, transmits the source code and optional standard input over the WebRTC `stream` DataChannel to Worker Node B, where it is compiled and executed in a sandboxed Docker container with:
- **`--network none`**: Disables container network access (air-gapped).
- **`--read-only`**: Read-only container root filesystem.
- **`--memory 128m --memory-swap 128m`**: 128 MB RAM limit.
- **`--cpus 1.0`**: 1 CPU core allocation.
- **`--pids-limit 64`**: Mitigates fork bombs.
- **`--cap-drop ALL`**: Drops all Linux capabilities.
- **`--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`**: Prevents setuid privilege elevation.
- **`--tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=64m`**: Ephemeral memory scratchpad.

---

### 9.5 Objective 3: GPU Acceleration & Resource Governance

Objective 3 adds GPU hardware capability discovery, 50 ms battery/activity watchdog preemption, and memory governance on Linux. When running `unicompute-node`, activate GPU features using:

```bash
./bin/unicompute-node -id node-A -signaling wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws -enable-gpu -gpu-backend auto -gpu-mem-limit-mb 2048 -gpu-watchdog-poll-ms 50
```

#### Node Flags for GPU Subsystem:
| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-enable-gpu` | `false` | Enables GPU capability probing, 50 ms watchdog, and memory limits. |
| `-gpu-backend` | `auto` | Preferred compute backend: `auto`, `cuda`, `directml`. |
| `-gpu-mem-limit-mb` | `2048` | Process memory ceiling in MB. |
| `-gpu-watchdog-poll-ms` | `50` | Watchdog polling frequency in ms (battery and idle monitoring). |
| `-gpu-ignore-battery` | `false` | Bypass battery check for AC-connected servers and desktop nodes. |

#### Interactive CLI Commands for GPU:
1. **`gpu`**: Displays real-time GPU hardware telemetry and 50 ms watchdog status:
   ```text
   > gpu
   ======================= Objective 3: GPU Hardware & Governance =======================
    Device Name:        NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 / AMD Radeon Graphics
    Vendor:             NVIDIA / AMD
    Total VRAM:         6141 MB
    Available VRAM:     5920 MB
    GPU Temperature:    45.0 °C | Power: 7.9 W
    Backends Detected:  [CPU DirectML CUDA]
   --------------------------------- 50 ms Watchdog State ---------------------------------
    Watchdog Status:    running
    Power Source:       OnBattery=false (100% remaining)
    User Activity:      Active=false (Idle: 15m20s)
   =======================================================================================
   ```

2. **`hipify <file.cu>`**: Analyzes CUDA kernels for 32-thread warp assumptions (`threadIdx.x % 32`, `__shfl_down_sync`) and translates portable kernels to HIP C++:
   ```text
   > hipify samples/gpu/portable_vector_add.cu
   [SUCCESS] Kernel successfully translated to portable HIP C++ (7 replacements made).
   ```

3. **`gpu-run <c|cpp|onnx> <file> [batches]`**: Executes workloads with memory and priority limits.
