package transport

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/pion/webrtc/v3"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/instrumentation"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/protocol"
	"github.com/unicompute/obj1/pkg/signaling"
)

func TestTransport_WebRTCConnectionAndChunkTransfer(t *testing.T) {
	// Start signaling hub
	hub, err := signaling.NewHub("127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start signaling hub: %v", err)
	}
	defer hub.Close()

	wsURL := hub.URL()

	trackerA := instrumentation.NewTracker()
	trackerB := instrumentation.NewTracker()

	var mgrAVal, mgrBVal atomic.Pointer[Manager]

	// Signaling client for Node A
	sigA, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-A", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrAVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigA: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigA.Close()

	// Signaling client for Node B
	sigB, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-B", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrBVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigB: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigB.Close()

	mgrA, err := NewManager(Config{
		NodeID: "node-A",
	}, sigA, trackerA)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrA: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrA.Close()
	mgrAVal.Store(mgrA)

	mgrB, err := NewManager(Config{
		NodeID: "node-B",
	}, sigB, trackerB)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrB: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrB.Close()
	mgrBVal.Store(mgrB)

	// Capture incoming connection on Node B
	connBChan := make(chan *PeerConnection, 1)
	mgrB.SetOnNewConnection(func(pc *PeerConnection) {
		connBChan <- pc
	})

	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) // Allow registrations to complete

	// Node A connects to Node B
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	connA, err := mgrA.ConnectPeer(ctx, "node-B")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ConnectPeer failed: %v", err)
	}
	defer connA.Close()

	var connB *PeerConnection
	select {
	case connB = <-connBChan:
	case <-ctx.Done():
		t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for incoming connection on Node B")
	}
	defer connB.Close()

	if err := connB.WaitConnected(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB failed to reach connected: %v", err)
	}
	if err := connB.WaitChannelsReady(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB channels not ready: %v", err)
	}

	// 1. Test Stream Channel
	streamMsg := []byte("stream log from A to B")
	receivedStreamCh := make(chan []byte, 1)
	connB.SetOnStreamMessage(func(msg []byte) {
		receivedStreamCh <- msg
	})

	if err := connA.SendStreamMessage(streamMsg); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendStreamMessage failed: %v", err)
	}

	select {
	case got := <-receivedStreamCh:
		if !bytes.Equal(got, streamMsg) {
			t.Errorf("stream message mismatch: got %q, want %q", string(got), string(streamMsg))
		}
	case <-time.After(2 * time.Second):
		t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for stream message")
	}

	// 2. Test Chunk Channel (Bulk Data Transfer)
	chunkData := bytes.Repeat([]byte("UniCompute chunk payload verification test bytes! "), 1000) // ~50 KB
	chunkHash := sha256.Sum256(chunkData)
	chunkID := hex.EncodeToString(chunkHash[:])

	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	var receivedData []byte
	var recvErr error

	wg.Add(1)
	go func() {
		defer wg.Done()
		recvCtx, recvCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
		defer recvCancel()
		receivedData, recvErr = connB.ReceiveChunk(recvCtx, chunkID, int64(len(chunkData)))
	}()

	time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)

	sendCtx, sendCancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
	defer sendCancel()
	err = connA.SendChunk(sendCtx, chunkID, bytes.NewReader(chunkData), int64(len(chunkData)))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("SendChunk failed: %v", err)
	}

	wg.Wait()

	if recvErr != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ReceiveChunk failed: %v", recvErr)
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(receivedData, chunkData) {
		t.Fatalf("received chunk payload mismatch")
	}

	// 3. Test Path Instrumentation
	time.Sleep(50 * time.Millisecond)
	mA, okA := trackerA.GetMetrics("node-B")
	if !okA {
		t.Fatalf("expected metrics for node-B on trackerA")
	}
	if mA.BytesSent <= 0 {
		t.Errorf("expected BytesSent > 0, got %d", mA.BytesSent)
	}
}

func TestUnnormalizedSTUN_ThrowsSchemeError(t *testing.T) {
	api := webrtc.NewAPI()
	// Raw unnormalized URL without scheme reproduces pion's "InvalidAccessError: unknown scheme type"
	rawCfg := webrtc.Configuration{
		ICEServers: []webrtc.ICEServer{
			{URLs: []string{"stun.l.google.com:19302"}},
		},
	}
	_, err := api.NewPeerConnection(rawCfg)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected NewPeerConnection to fail with raw host:port, but it succeeded")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "unknown scheme type") {
		t.Errorf("expected 'unknown scheme type' error, got %v", err)
	}
}

func TestBuildICEServers_AndPeerConnectionCreation(t *testing.T) {
	testCases := []struct {
		name        string
		stunServers []string
		turnServers []TURNServerConfig
		wantSTUN    []string
		wantTURN    []string
	}{
		{
			name:        "Bare host and port STUN",
			stunServers: []string{"stun.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name:        "Prefixed stun: host and port",
			stunServers: []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name:        "Double slash stun:// syntax",
			stunServers: []string{"stun://stun.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name:        "Uppercase STUN: scheme",
			stunServers: []string{"STUN:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name:        "STUNS secure scheme",
			stunServers: []string{"stuns:stun.l.google.com:5349"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stuns:stun.l.google.com:5349"},
		},
		{
			name:        "Double slash stuns:// syntax",
			stunServers: []string{"stuns://stun.l.google.com:5349"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stuns:stun.l.google.com:5349"},
		},
		{
			name:        "Comma-separated STUN entries",
			stunServers: []string{"stun.l.google.com:19302, stun1.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN:    []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302", "stun:stun1.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name: "Bare TURN URL",
			turnServers: []TURNServerConfig{
				{URL: "relay.unicompute.org:3478", Username: "user", Credential: "pwd"},
			},
			wantTURN: []string{"turn:relay.unicompute.org:3478"},
		},
		{
			name: "Double slash turn:// URL",
			turnServers: []TURNServerConfig{
				{URL: "turn://relay.unicompute.org:3478", Username: "user", Credential: "pwd"},
			},
			wantTURN: []string{"turn:relay.unicompute.org:3478"},
		},
		{
			name: "TURNS secure scheme",
			turnServers: []TURNServerConfig{
				{URL: "turns://relay.unicompute.org:5349", Username: "user", Credential: "pwd"},
			},
			wantTURN: []string{"turns:relay.unicompute.org:5349"},
		},
		{
			name: "Whitespace after stun prefix",
			stunServers: []string{"stun:   stun.l.google.com:19302"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com:19302"},
		},
		{
			name: "Comma-separated TURN URLs",
			turnServers: []TURNServerConfig{
				{URL: "turn:relay1.unicompute.org:3478, turn:relay2.unicompute.org:3478", Username: "user", Credential: "pwd"},
			},
			wantTURN: []string{"turn:relay1.unicompute.org:3478", "turn:relay2.unicompute.org:3478"},
		},
		{
			name: "Empty and malformed STUN strings",
			stunServers: []string{"", "   ", "stun:", "stun://", " ,  "},
			wantSTUN: nil,
		},
		{
			name: "IPv6 STUN with brackets and port",
			stunServers: []string{"[::1]:19302"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:[::1]:19302"},
		},
		{
			name: "IPv6 STUN with brackets without port",
			stunServers: []string{"[::1]"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:[::1]"},
		},
		{
			name: "STUN without port",
			stunServers: []string{"stun.l.google.com"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:stun.l.google.com"},
		},
		{
			name: "IPv6 bare without brackets with port",
			stunServers: []string{"2001:db8::1:19302"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:[2001:db8::1]:19302"},
		},
		{
			name: "IPv6 bare without brackets without port",
			stunServers: []string{"2001:db8::1"},
			wantSTUN: []string{"stun:[2001:db8::1]"},
		},
	}

	for _, tc := range testCases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			mgr, err := NewManager(Config{
				NodeID:      "test-node",
				STUNServers: tc.stunServers,
				TURNServers: tc.turnServers,
			}, nil, nil)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("NewManager failed: %v", err)
			}
			defer mgr.Close()

			iceServers := mgr.buildICEServers()

			// Verify that Pion NewPeerConnection succeeds without 'unknown scheme type' error
			webrtcCfg := webrtc.Configuration{
				ICEServers: iceServers,
			}
			pc, err := mgr.api.NewPeerConnection(webrtcCfg)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("NewPeerConnection failed with normalized ICEServers: %v", err)
			}
			_ = pc.Close()

			if len(tc.wantSTUN) > 0 {
				if len(iceServers) == 0 {
					t.Fatalf("expected at least 1 ICEServer for STUN")
				}
				if len(iceServers[0].URLs) != len(tc.wantSTUN) {
					t.Errorf("got %d STUN URLs, want %d", len(iceServers[0].URLs), len(tc.wantSTUN))
				}
				for i, u := range tc.wantSTUN {
					if i < len(iceServers[0].URLs) && iceServers[0].URLs[i] != u {
						t.Errorf("STUN URL[%d] = %q, want %q", i, iceServers[0].URLs[i], u)
					}
				}
			}

			if len(tc.wantTURN) > 0 {
				turnIdx := 0
				if len(tc.wantSTUN) > 0 {
					turnIdx = 1
				}
				if len(iceServers) <= turnIdx {
					t.Fatalf("expected ICEServer for TURN at index %d", turnIdx)
				}
				if len(iceServers[turnIdx].URLs) != len(tc.wantTURN) {
					t.Errorf("got %d TURN URLs, want %d", len(iceServers[turnIdx].URLs), len(tc.wantTURN))
				}
				for i, u := range tc.wantTURN {
					if i < len(iceServers[turnIdx].URLs) && iceServers[turnIdx].URLs[i] != u {
						t.Errorf("TURN URL[%d] = %q, want %q", i, iceServers[turnIdx].URLs[i], u)
					}
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestPeerSessionEvictionOnClose(t *testing.T) {
	hub, err := signaling.NewHub("127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start signaling hub: %v", err)
	}
	defer hub.Close()

	wsURL := hub.URL()

	var mgrAVal, mgrBVal atomic.Pointer[Manager]

	sigA, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-evict-A", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrAVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigA: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigA.Close()

	sigB, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-evict-B", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrBVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigB: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigB.Close()

	mgrA, err := NewManager(Config{NodeID: "node-evict-A"}, sigA, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrA: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrA.Close()
	mgrAVal.Store(mgrA)

	mgrB, err := NewManager(Config{NodeID: "node-evict-B"}, sigB, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrB: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrB.Close()
	mgrBVal.Store(mgrB)

	connBChan := make(chan *PeerConnection, 1)
	mgrB.SetOnNewConnection(func(pc *PeerConnection) {
		connBChan <- pc
	})

	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	connA, err := mgrA.ConnectPeer(ctx, "node-evict-B")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ConnectPeer failed: %v", err)
	}
	defer connA.Close()

	var connB *PeerConnection
	select {
	case connB = <-connBChan:
	case <-ctx.Done():
		t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for incoming connection on Node B")
	}

	if err := connB.WaitConnected(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB failed to connect: %v", err)
	}
	if err := connB.WaitChannelsReady(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB channels not ready: %v", err)
	}

	// Verify active connection exists
	if _, ok := mgrA.GetConnection("node-evict-B"); !ok {
		t.Fatalf("expected mgrA to have connection to node-evict-B")
	}
	peers := mgrA.ActivePeers()
	if len(peers) == 0 || peers[0] != "node-evict-B" {
		t.Fatalf("expected node-evict-B in ActivePeers, got %v", peers)
	}

	// Close remote peer connB and verify eviction from mgrA
	_ = connB.Close()

	deadline := time.Now().Add(10 * time.Second)
	evicted := false
	for time.Now().Before(deadline) {
		_, ok := mgrA.GetConnection("node-evict-B")
		if !ok && len(mgrA.ActivePeers()) == 0 {
			evicted = true
			break
		}
		time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond)
	}

	if !evicted {
		t.Errorf("expected peer session to be evicted from mgrA after connection closed")
	}
	_ = connB.Close()
}

func TestZeroByteChunkTransfer(t *testing.T) {
	hub, err := signaling.NewHub("127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start signaling hub: %v", err)
	}
	defer hub.Close()

	wsURL := hub.URL()

	var mgrAVal, mgrBVal atomic.Pointer[Manager]

	sigA, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-chunk-A", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrAVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigA: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigA.Close()

	sigB, err := signaling.NewClient(wsURL, "node-chunk-B", func(env protocol.Envelope) {
		if env.Type != protocol.MsgRegisterAck {
			if m := mgrBVal.Load(); m != nil {
				_ = m.HandleSignalingEnvelope(env)
			}
		}
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to start sigB: %v", err)
	}
	defer sigB.Close()

	mgrA, err := NewManager(Config{NodeID: "node-chunk-A"}, sigA, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrA: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrA.Close()
	mgrAVal.Store(mgrA)

	mgrB, err := NewManager(Config{NodeID: "node-chunk-B"}, sigB, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("failed to create mgrB: %v", err)
	}
	defer mgrB.Close()
	mgrBVal.Store(mgrB)

	connBChan := make(chan *PeerConnection, 1)
	mgrB.SetOnNewConnection(func(pc *PeerConnection) {
		connBChan <- pc
	})

	time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond)

	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
	defer cancel()

	connA, err := mgrA.ConnectPeer(ctx, "node-chunk-B")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ConnectPeer failed: %v", err)
	}
	defer connA.Close()

	var connB *PeerConnection
	select {
	case connB = <-connBChan:
	case <-ctx.Done():
		t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for incoming connection on Node B")
	}
	defer connB.Close()

	if err := connB.WaitConnected(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB failed to connect: %v", err)
	}
	if err := connB.WaitChannelsReady(ctx); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("connB channels not ready: %v", err)
	}

	zeroChunkID := "e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855"
	connB.SetOnChunkRequest(func(chunkID string) {
		if chunkID == zeroChunkID {
			_ = connB.SendChunk(ctx, chunkID, bytes.NewReader([]byte{}), 0)
		}
	})

	data, err := connA.FetchChunk(ctx, zeroChunkID, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("FetchChunk failed for 0-byte chunk: %v", err)
	}
	if len(data) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("expected 0 bytes, got %d bytes", len(data))
	}
}

$PSScriptRoot = Split-Path -Parent $MyInvocation.MyCommand.Path

Write-Host "  UniCompute Desktop Control Room (Objectives 1, 2, 3)" -ForegroundColor Cyan

# Locate executable

if (Test-Path "$PSScriptRoot\unicompute-gui.exe") {
    $guiExe = "$PSScriptRoot\unicompute-gui.exe"

    $guiExe = "$PSScriptRoot\bin\unicompute-gui.exe"
}

if (-not $guiExe) {
    if (Get-Command go -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        Write-Host "unicompute-gui.exe not found. Compiling GUI binary..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
        New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "$PSScriptRoot\bin" | Out-Null
        $env:CGO_ENABLED = "0"
        & go build -o "$PSScriptRoot\bin\unicompute-gui.exe" "$PSScriptRoot\cmd\unicompute-gui"
        if (Test-Path "$PSScriptRoot\bin\unicompute-gui.exe") {
            $guiExe = "$PSScriptRoot\bin\unicompute-gui.exe"
        }
    }
}

if (-not $guiExe) {
    Write-Host "[ERROR] Could not find unicompute-gui.exe in root or bin/" -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}

if ($Id) { $guiArgs += @("-id", $Id) }
if ($Signaling) { $guiArgs += @("-signaling", $Signaling) }
if ($Headless) { $guiArgs += @("-headless") }

$pkgs = @("blobstore", "codeexec", "instrumentation", "nat", "relay", "remoteshell", "signaling", "transport", "node")
$allPassed = $true

New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "bin" | Out-Null

$cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\CurrentUser\My -CodeSigningCert -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $cert) {
    $cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -Type CodeSigningCert -Subject "CN=UniCompute Dev" -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
}

foreach ($p in $pkgs) {
    Write-Host "`n--> Testing pkg/$p" -ForegroundColor Yellow
    
    # Try direct go test first
    $testOutput = go test -v "./pkg/$p" 2>&1
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
        $testOutput | Out-String | Write-Host
        continue
    }
    
    # If direct go test failed due to AppControl on temp binary, compile locally into bin/ and run
    Write-Host "Direct go test exited ($LASTEXITCODE), falling back to local bin build..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    $exeName = "bin/unicompute_${p}_test.exe"
    go test -c -o $exeName "./pkg/$p"
    if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0) {
        if ($cert) {
            Set-AuthenticodeSignature -Certificate $cert -FilePath $exeName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null
        }
        & ".\$exeName" "-test.v"
        if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
            $allPassed = $false
        }
        Remove-Item $exeName -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    } else {
        $allPassed = $false
    }
}

if ($allPassed) {
    Write-Host "`n[SUCCESS] All Objective 1 tests passed!" -ForegroundColor Green
} else {
    Write-Host "`n[FAILURE] One or more test suites failed." -ForegroundColor Red
    exit 1
}

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>

// Simple 32-bit FNV-1a hash function
uint32_t fnv1a_32(const char* s) {
    uint32_t hash = 2166136261u;
    while (*s) {
        hash ^= (uint8_t)(*s++);
        hash *= 16777619u;
    }
    return hash;
}

int main(void) {
    const char* messages[] = {
        "UniCompute Objective 1: P2P Transport Substrate",
        "Dual-Stack ICE & CGNAT Hole-Punching Subsystem",
        "Content-Addressed CAS Blob Store Vault",
        "Air-Gapped Docker Container Code Sandbox",
        "WebRTC Bidirectional DataChannel Multiplexing"
    };
    int count = sizeof(messages) / sizeof(messages[0]);

    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf("     UniCompute Worker: C Runtime Verification    \n");
    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf("C Standard : ISO C17 (GCC 14)\n");
    printf("Target OS  : Linux Container (x86_64 / arm64)\n");
    printf("--------------------------------------------------\n");

    for (int i = 0; i < count; i++) {
        uint32_t hash = fnv1a_32(messages[i]);
        printf("[%d] %-48s | FNV-1a: 0x%08X\n", i + 1, messages[i], hash);
    }

    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf("Status: C worker execution passed.\n");
    return 0;
}

FILE: samples/c/system_info.c
================================================
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <time.h>

/*
 * UniCompute Objective 2 Sample: C Benchmark & System Diagnostics
 * Performs memory allocation, integer throughput hashing, and pointer alignment checks.
 */

#define BENCHMARK_ITEMS 65536

uint32_t murmur3_32(const uint8_t* key, size_t len, uint32_t seed) {
    uint32_t h = seed;
    uint32_t c1 = 0xcc9e2d51;
    uint32_t c2 = 0x1b873593;
    const int nblocks = len / 4;
    const uint32_t *blocks = (const uint32_t *)(key);

    for (int i = 0; i < nblocks; i++) {
        uint32_t k = blocks[i];
        k *= c1;
        k = (k << 15) | (k >> (32 - 15));
        k *= c2;

        h ^= k;
        h = (h << 13) | (h >> (32 - 13));
        h = h * 5 + 0xe6546b64;
    }

    h ^= len;
    h ^= h >> 16;
    h *= 0x85ebca6b;
    h ^= h >> 13;
    h *= 0xc2b2ae35;
    h ^= h >> 16;
    return h;
}

int main(void) {
    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf("   UniCompute Worker: C Memory & Hash Benchmark   \n");
    printf("==================================================\n");

    printf("Word Size     : %zu bits (%zu bytes)\n", sizeof(void*) * 8, sizeof(void*));
    printf("Integer Width : %zu bits\n", sizeof(int) * 8);
    printf("Pointer Size  : %zu bytes\n", sizeof(void*));

    size_t alloc_bytes = BENCHMARK_ITEMS * sizeof(uint32_t);
    printf("Allocating    : %zu bytes (%.2f KiB) heap buffer...\n", alloc_bytes, (double)alloc_bytes / 1024.0);

    uint32_t* buffer = (uint32_t*)malloc(alloc_bytes);
    if (!buffer) {
        fprintf(stderr, "[ERROR] Memory allocation failed!\n");
        return 1;
    }

    clock_t start = clock();
    for (size_t i = 0; i < BENCHMARK_ITEMS; i++) {
        buffer[i] = (uint32_t)(i ^ (i << 13) ^ (i >> 17));
    }

    uint32_t hash = murmur3_32((const uint8_t*)buffer, alloc_bytes, 0x9747b28c);
    clock_t end = clock();
    double duration_ms = ((double)(end - start) / CLOCKS_PER_SEC) * 1000.0;

    printf("--------------------------------------------------\n");
    printf("Items Hashed  : %d 32-bit words\n", BENCHMARK_ITEMS);
    printf("Murmur3 Check : 0x%08X\n", hash);
    printf("Duration      : %.2f ms\n", duration_ms);
    printf("Throughput    : %.2f MB/s\n", ((double)alloc_bytes / (1024.0 * 1024.0)) / (duration_ms / 1000.0 + 1e-6));
    printf("==================================================\n");
    printf("Status: C worker execution passed.\n");

    free(buffer);
    return 0;
}

FILE: samples/cpp/fib.cpp

#include <iostream>
#include <vector>
#include <iomanip>
#include <chrono>

// Compute Fibonacci numbers iteratively and calculate ratios approaching Golden Ratio
void computeFibonacci(int count) {
    std::cout << "==================================================" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "    UniCompute Worker: C++ Fibonacci Benchmark    " << std::endl;
    std::cout << "==================================================" << std::endl;

    if (count <= 0) return;
    
    std::vector<unsigned long long> fib;
    fib.reserve(count);
    fib.push_back(0);
    if (count > 1) fib.push_back(1);

    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();

    for (int i = 2; i < count; ++i) {
        fib.push_back(fib[i - 1] + fib[i - 2]);
    }

    auto elapsed = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::microseconds>(
        std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now() - start
    ).count();

    std::cout << "First " << count << " Fibonacci numbers computed in " << elapsed << " microseconds:\n\n";
    for (int i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
        std::cout << std::setw(3) << i << ": " << std::setw(20) << fib[i];
        if (i > 1 && fib[i - 1] > 0) {
            double ratio = static_cast<double>(fib[i]) / static_cast<double>(fib[i - 1]);
            std::cout << "  (Ratio: " << std::fixed << std::setprecision(8) << ratio << ")";
        }
        std::cout << "\n";
    }

    std::cout << "==================================================" << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Approaching Golden Ratio (phi): 1.6180339887..." << std::endl;
    std::cout << "Status: C++ computation completed successfully." << std::endl;
}

int main() {
    computeFibonacci(45);
    return 0;
}

# Objective 3 GPU Test Sample Data & Verification Suite

This directory contains test kernels and workload inputs for validating **UniCompute Objective 3 (Cross-Platform GPU Acceleration and Resource Governance)**.

---

## Sample Data Files

| File | Type | Target Hardware | Purpose & Expected Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|
| `portable_vector_add.cu` | CUDA C++ Kernel | NVIDIA & AMD | Standard portable vector addition. Tests automated HIPIFY translation (`cudaMalloc` $\rightarrow$ `hipMalloc`, `cudaFree` $\rightarrow$ `hipFree`). Marked **PASS/Portable** for AMD execution. |
| `warp_reduction.cu` | CUDA C++ Kernel | NVIDIA Only | Implements tree reduction using `__shfl_down_sync` and `threadIdx.x % 32`. Triggers static analysis blocker on AMD 64-thread wavefronts. Marked **REJECTED** with diagnostic line pointers. |
| `inline_ptx.cu` | CUDA C++ Kernel | NVIDIA Only | Contains inline PTX assembly (`asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %smid;")`). Triggers ROCm compiler incompatibility blocker. Marked **REJECTED** with recommendation to export to ONNX. |
| `test_model.json` | ONNX Metadata | DirectML & CUDA | Tensor layer definition and weights for validating forward FP32 preprocessing and execution. |

---

## Quick Verification Commands

### 1. Test Automated CUDA Translation
```text
> hipify ./samples/gpu/portable_vector_add.cu
```
*Expected*: Success report, 7 replacements made, preview of translated `#include <hip/hip_runtime.h>` code.

### 2. Test Warp Incompatibility Detection
```text
> hipify ./samples/gpu/warp_reduction.cu
```
*Expected*: Diagnostic warning on Line 4 (`threadIdx.x % 32`) and Line 9 (`__shfl_down_sync`), blocking translation to prevent runtime errors on AMD GPUs.

### 3. Test Inline PTX Detection
```text
> hipify ./samples/gpu/inline_ptx.cu
```
*Expected*: Diagnostic error on Line 6 flagging inline PTX assembly.

### 4. Test JobObject Sandboxed Execution
```text
> gpu-run cpp ./samples/gpu/portable_vector_add.cu 50
```
*Expected*: Execution completes inside the Win32 JobObject sandbox under `IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS` with bounded memory.

FILE: samples/gpu/inline_ptx.cu

#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__device__ unsigned int getSpecialRegister() {
    unsigned int reg;
    // Inline PTX assembly (cannot compile under ROCm/HIP)
    asm volatile("mov.u32 %0, %smid;" : "=r"(reg));
    return reg;
}

__global__ void ptxKernel(unsigned int *out) {
    if (threadIdx.x == 0) {
        out[blockIdx.x] = getSpecialRegister();
    }
}

FILE: samples/gpu/matrix_transpose.cu

/*
 * UniCompute Objective 3 Sample: Shared Memory Matrix Transpose
 * Portable CUDA kernel demonstrating 2D thread block indexing and __syncthreads().
 * Valid for translation via HIPIFY to AMD ROCm / HIP.
 */

#define TILE_DIM 32
#define BLOCK_ROWS 8

__global__ void transposeCoalesced(float *odata, const float *idata, int width, int height) {
    __shared__ float tile[TILE_DIM][TILE_DIM + 1]; // +1 prevents bank conflicts

    int x = blockIdx.x * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.x;
    int y = blockIdx.y * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.y;

    for (int j = 0; j < TILE_DIM; j += BLOCK_ROWS) {
        if (x < width && (y + j) < height) {
            tile[threadIdx.y + j][threadIdx.x] = idata[(y + j) * width + x];
        }
    }

    __syncthreads();

    x = blockIdx.y * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.x;
    y = blockIdx.x * TILE_DIM + threadIdx.y;

    for (int j = 0; j < TILE_DIM; j += BLOCK_ROWS) {
        if (x < height && (y + j) < width) {
            odata[(y + j) * height + x] = tile[threadIdx.x][threadIdx.y + j];
        }
    }
}

#include <cuda_runtime.h>
#include <stdio.h>

__global__ void vectorAdd(const float *a, const float *b, float *c, int n) {
    int i = blockDim.x * blockIdx.x + threadIdx.x;
    if (i < n) {
        c[i] = a[i] + b[i];
    }
}

int main() {
    int n = 1024;
    size_t size = n * sizeof(float);
    float *d_a, *d_b, *d_c;
    cudaMalloc(&d_a, size);
    cudaMalloc(&d_b, size);
    cudaMalloc(&d_c, size);
    cudaFree(d_a);
    cudaFree(d_b);
    cudaFree(d_c);
    return 0;
}

FILE: samples/gpu/warp_reduction.cu
================================================
#include <cuda_runtime.h>

__global__ void warpReduction(float *d_out, float *d_in) {
    int lane = threadIdx.x % 32; // Assuming 32-thread warp
    float val = d_in[threadIdx.x];

    // Warp-level shuffle intrinsic (fails on AMD 64-thread wavefront)
    for (int offset = 16; offset > 0; offset /= 2) {
        val += __shfl_down_sync(0xffffffff, val, offset);
    }

    if (lane == 0) {
        d_out[blockIdx.x] = val;
    }
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import math

def process_stream():
    numbers = []
    print("==================================================")
    print("   UniCompute Worker: Python Data Processing Job  ")
    print("==================================================")
    raw_input = sys.stdin.read().lstrip('\ufeff')
    if not raw_input.strip():
        print("[WARN] No input received on stdin. Generating default test data.")
        numbers = [42.0, 17.5, 88.2, 9.1, 104.6, 55.0, 31.4, 76.9]
    else:
        for token in raw_input.split():
            try:
                numbers.append(float(token))
            except ValueError:
                pass

    if not numbers:
        print("[ERROR] No valid numbers found in input stream.")
        return

    n = len(numbers)
    total_sum = sum(numbers)
    mean = total_sum / n
    variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in numbers) / n
    std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)
    min_val = min(numbers)
    max_val = max(numbers)
    sorted_nums = sorted(numbers)
    median = sorted_nums[n // 2] if n % 2 != 0 else (sorted_nums[n // 2 - 1] + sorted_nums[n // 2]) / 2.0

    print(f"Records Processed : {n}")
    print(f"Sum               : {total_sum:.4f}")
    print(f"Mean (Average)    : {mean:.4f}")
    print(f"Median            : {median:.4f}")
    print(f"Standard Dev      : {std_dev:.4f}")
    print(f"Minimum Value     : {min_val:.4f}")
    print(f"Maximum Value     : {max_val:.4f}")
    print(f"Sorted First 5    : {sorted_nums[:5]}")
    print(f"Sorted Last 5     : {sorted_nums[-5:]}")
    print("==================================================")
    print("Status: Calculation completed successfully.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    process_stream()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UniCompute Objective 2 Sample: Matrix Multiplication Benchmark
Demonstrates floating-point matrix multiplication with validation and optional stdin dimension override.
"""
import sys
import time

def matrix_multiply(dim=64):
    print("==================================================")
    print(" UniCompute Worker: Matrix Multiplication (O2)   ")
    print("==================================================")
    
    # Read matrix dimension from stdin if provided
    raw = sys.stdin.read().strip()
    if raw.isdigit():
        dim = max(8, min(256, int(raw)))
        print(f"[INPUT] Using stdin matrix dimension: {dim}x{dim}")
    else:
        print(f"[INFO] Using default dimension: {dim}x{dim}")

    print(f"Allocating two {dim}x{dim} floating-point matrices...")
    A = [[(i * dim + j) * 0.001 for j in range(dim)] for i in range(dim)]
    B = [[(j * dim + i) * 0.001 for j in range(dim)] for i in range(dim)]
    C = [[0.0 for _ in range(dim)] for _ in range(dim)]

    t0 = time.time()
    for i in range(dim):
        for k in range(dim):
            aik = A[i][k]
            for j in range(dim):
                C[i][j] += aik * B[k][j]
    elapsed = time.time() - t0

    # Verification checksum
    trace = sum(C[i][i] for i in range(dim))
    corner_sum = C[0][0] + C[0][-1] + C[-1][0] + C[-1][-1]
    gflops = (2.0 * dim * dim * dim) / (elapsed * 1e9) if elapsed > 0 else 0.0

    print("--------------------------------------------------")
    print(f"Matrix Dimension : {dim} x {dim}")
    print(f"Total Operations : {2 * dim**3:,} FLOPs")
    print(f"Compute Duration : {elapsed * 1000.0:.2f} ms")
    print(f"Performance      : {gflops * 1000.0:.2f} MFLOP/s")
    print(f"Matrix Trace     : {trace:.6f}")
    print(f"Corners Checksum : {corner_sum:.6f}")
    print("==================================================")
    print("Status: Matrix multiplication completed successfully.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    matrix_multiply()

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UniCompute Security Test: Memory Limit Enforcement (128 MB Cap)
Verifies that the Docker container sandbox enforces '--memory 128m --memory-swap 128m'.
Continuously allocates 10 MB blocks in RAM until the container is capped
by the Linux OOM (Out Of Memory) killer or raises MemoryError.
"""

import sys
import time

print("==================================================")
print("  UniCompute Security: 128 MB RAM Limit Audit     ")
print("==================================================")
print("Allocating memory in 10 MB chunks...")

chunks = []
total_mb = 0

try:
    for step in range(1, 30):
        # Allocate 10 MB of real dirty pages (not just virtual space)
        chunk = bytearray(10 * 1024 * 1024)
        # Touch every page so the kernel actually commits the RAM
        for i in range(0, len(chunk), 4096):
            chunk[i] = 0xFF
        chunks.append(chunk)
        total_mb += 10
        print(f"[ALLOCATION] Successfully allocated {total_mb} MB RAM", flush=True)
        time.sleep(0.05)

    print(f"[FAIL] Allocated {total_mb} MB without hitting the 128 MB container cap!")
    sys.exit(1)

except MemoryError:
    print(f"\n[PASS] Python raised MemoryError after allocating {total_mb} MB.")
    print("RESULT: MEMORY CAPPING ENFORCED SUCCESSFULLY.")
    sys.exit(0)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
UniCompute Security Test: Network Leak / Air-Gap Verification
Verifies that Docker container sandbox enforces '--network none'.
Attempts outbound TCP socket connection and HTTP fetch to public targets.
If any network access succeeds, the test FAILS (security breach).
If network access is blocked/unreachable, the test PASSES (air-gap intact).
"""

import socket
import sys
import urllib.request
import urllib.error

print("==================================================")
print("  UniCompute Security: Network Air-Gap Audit     ")
print("==================================================")

passed = True

# Test 1: Raw TCP socket connect to 1.1.1.1:80
print("[TEST 1] Probing outbound TCP socket to 1.1.1.1:80 ...")
s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.settimeout(2.0)
try:
    s.connect(("1.1.1.1", 80))
    print("[FAIL] CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: Outbound socket connection succeeded!")
    passed = False
except (OSError, socket.error) as e:
    print(f"[PASS] Socket connection blocked as expected: {e}")
finally:
    s.close()

# Test 2: Outbound DNS resolution for public hostname
print("[TEST 2] Probing outbound DNS resolution for example.com ...")
try:
    resolved_ip = socket.gethostbyname("example.com")
    print(f"[FAIL] CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: DNS resolution succeeded (resolved to {resolved_ip})!")
    passed = False
except (socket.gaierror, OSError) as e:
    print(f"[PASS] DNS resolution blocked as expected: {e}")


# Test 3: HTTP request attempt via urllib
print("[TEST 3] Probing outbound HTTP request to http://example.com ...")
try:
    with urllib.request.urlopen("http://example.com", timeout=2.0) as resp:
        print("[FAIL] CRITICAL SECURITY ISSUE: HTTP request succeeded!")
        passed = False
except Exception as e:
    print(f"[PASS] HTTP request blocked as expected: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")

print("==================================================")
if passed:
    print("RESULT: AIR-GAP VERIFICATION PASSED. Container is completely isolated.")
    sys.exit(0)
else:
    print("RESULT: AIR-GAP VERIFICATION FAILED. Container leaked network packets.")
    sys.exit(1)

UniCompute Security Test: Execution Timeout Enforcement
Tests worker enforcement of container runtime bounds (default 10s - 15s).
This script deliberately executes an infinite loop with sleep to verify
that the worker forcibly kills the container and reports a timeout status.
"""

import time
import sys

print("[SECURITY TEST] Starting infinite compute/sleep loop...", flush=True)
print("[SECURITY TEST] Worker policy must terminate container after timeout.", flush=True)

elapsed = 0
while True:
    time.sleep(1)
    elapsed += 1
    print(f"[SECURITY TEST] Elapsed: {elapsed} seconds (still running)...", flush=True)

# =======================================================================
#  UniCompute Master Verification Suite (Objectives 1, 2, 3 & Samples)
# =======================================================================

$startTime = Get-Date
$scorecard = @()
$script:allPassed = $true

# Use system Go directly

$codeCert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\CurrentUser\My -CodeSigningCert -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Where-Object { $_.Thumbprint -eq "0B7334834AEBC5CD9D649685669D9AC4DAC77DCC" } | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $codeCert) {
    $codeCert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\CurrentUser\My -CodeSigningCert -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
}
if (-not $codeCert) {
    try {
        $codeCert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -Type CodeSigningCert -Subject "CN=UniCompute Dev" -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My" -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    } catch {}
}
function Sign-Binary {
    param([string]$Path)
    if ($codeCert -and (Test-Path $Path)) {
        try { Set-AuthenticodeSignature -Certificate $codeCert -FilePath $Path -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Out-Null } catch {}
    }
}

function Record-Result {
    param(
        [string]$Category,
        [string]$TestName,
        [bool]$Passed,
        [string]$Duration,
        [string]$Details
    )
    $obj = [PSCustomObject]@{
        Category = $Category
        TestName = $TestName
        Status   = if ($Passed) { "PASS" } else { "FAIL" }
        Duration = $Duration
        Details  = $Details
    }
    $script:scorecard += $obj
    if (-not $Passed) {
        $script:allPassed = $false
        Write-Host " [FAIL] $TestName ($Duration) - $Details" -ForegroundColor Red
    } else {
        Write-Host " [PASS] $TestName ($Duration)" -ForegroundColor Green
    }
}

)

    if ($passed) {

    } else {

    $sw.Stop()
    $passed = ($null -ne $putResp.blob_id) -and ($scrubResp.status -eq "complete") -and ($scrubResp.corrupted.Count -eq 0)
    Record-Result -Category "GUI API" -TestName "/api/storage/put & /scrub" -Passed $passed -Duration "$([math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds))ms" -Details "Blob ID=$($putResp.blob_id), Scrub Corrupted=0"

    # 4.6 GPU Sandboxed Run API
    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    $runResp = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:$testPort/api/gpu/run" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Headers $authHeaders -Body (@{ task_type = "gemm"; batches = 10 } | ConvertTo-Json)
    $sw.Stop()
    $passed = ($runResp.status -eq "completed") -and ($runResp.processed_batches -eq 10)
    Record-Result -Category "GUI API" -TestName "/api/gpu/run" -Passed $passed -Duration "$([math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds))ms" -Details "Batches=10, Time=$($runResp.execution_ms)ms"

    # 4.7 Web HTML Index Serving
    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    $htmlResp = Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:$testPort/" -UseBasicParsing
    $sw.Stop()
    $passed = ($htmlResp.StatusCode -eq 200) -and ($htmlResp.Content -like "*UniCompute*")
    Record-Result -Category "GUI API" -TestName "GET / (HTML5/Canvas)" -Passed $passed -Duration "$([math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds))ms" -Details "Control room frontend bundle served (Status 200)"

    # 4.8 Unauthenticated Shell Exec Rejection (401)
    $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
    $unauthBlocked = $false
    try {
        $null = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "http://127.0.0.1:$testPort/api/shell/exec" -Method Post -ContentType "application/json" -Body (@{ command = "echo test" } | ConvertTo-Json)
    } catch {
        if ($_.Exception.Response.StatusCode.value__ -eq 401 -or $_.Exception.Message -like "*401*") {
            $unauthBlocked = $true
        }
    }
    $sw.Stop()
    Record-Result -Category "GUI API" -TestName "/api/shell/exec (Unauthenticated 401)" -Passed $unauthBlocked -Duration "$([math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds))ms" -Details "Unauthenticated remote shell access rejected with 401 Unauthorized"

    # 4.9 Frontend JavaScript Syntax Verification
    if (Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
        $sw = [System.Diagnostics.Stopwatch]::StartNew()
        $nodeAppOut = node --check cmd/unicompute-gui/web/js/app.js 2>&1
        $appExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        $nodeTopoOut = node --check cmd/unicompute-gui/web/js/topology.js 2>&1
        $topoExit = $LASTEXITCODE
        $sw.Stop()
        $jsPassed = ($appExit -eq 0) -and ($topoExit -eq 0)
        Record-Result -Category "GUI API" -TestName "Frontend JS Syntax" -Passed $jsPassed -Duration "$([math]::Round($sw.Elapsed.TotalMilliseconds))ms" -Details "node --check on app.js and topology.js"
    }

} finally {
    Write-Host "`n--> Stopping GUI test daemon..." -ForegroundColor Yellow
    Get-Process -Name unicompute-gui -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Stop-Process -Force
    if ($guiProc -and -not $guiProc.HasExited) {
        Stop-Process -Id $guiProc.Id -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    }
    Remove-Item $guiLog -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Remove-Item $guiErrLog -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
    Start-Sleep -Milliseconds 500
}

Write-Host "`n=======================================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host " PHASE 5: COMPREHENSIVE VERIFICATION SCORECARD" -ForegroundColor Cyan
Write-Host "=======================================================================" -ForegroundColor Cyan

$scorecard | Format-Table -AutoSize Category, TestName, Status, Duration, Details

$totalTests = $scorecard.Count
$passedCount = ($scorecard | Where-Object { $_.Status -eq "PASS" }).Count
$failedCount = $totalTests - $passedCount
$totalDuration = "$([math]::Round(((Get-Date) - $startTime).TotalSeconds, 2))s"

Write-Host "`nSummary: $passedCount/$totalTests Passed ($failedCount Failed) in $totalDuration" -ForegroundColor $(if ($script:allPassed) { "Green" } else { "Red" })

if ($script:allPassed) {
    Write-Host "`n[SUCCESS] All subsystems, hardware tests, samples, and GUI endpoints verified 100%!" -ForegroundColor Green

# language: Python, file: test_pack.py, runtime: Python 3.10+, target: Unit tests for pack.py
import json
import os
import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

from pack import (
    is_existing_digest,
    is_binary_file,
    decode_text,
    clean_notebook_content,
    discover_project_files,
    pack_project,
    parse_args,
    GLOBAL_EXCLUDE_DIRS,
    EXCLUDE_EXTENSIONS,
    EXCLUDE_FILES,
    ALLOWED_DOTFILES
)


class TestPackDigest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.test_dir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="unicompute_pack_test_")
        self.root = Path(self.test_dir)

    def tearDown(self):
        shutil.rmtree(self.test_dir, ignore_errors=True)

    def test_is_existing_digest_variants(self):
        # 1. Standard Digest with LF
        digest_lf = b"Directory structure:\n  pkg/blobstore.go\n\n================================================\nFILE: pkg/blobstore.go\n================================================\ncontent\n"
        self.assertTrue(is_existing_digest(digest_lf))

        # 2. Standard Digest with CRLF
        digest_crlf = b"Directory structure:\r\n  pkg/blobstore.go\r\n\r\n================================================\r\nFILE: pkg/blobstore.go\r\n================================================\r\ncontent\r\n"
        self.assertTrue(is_existing_digest(digest_crlf))

        # 3. Digest with UTF-8 BOM (very common on Windows)
        digest_bom = b"\xef\xbb\xbfDirectory structure:\n  pkg/blobstore.go\n\n================================================\nFILE: pkg/blobstore.go\n================================================\ncontent\n"
        self.assertTrue(is_existing_digest(digest_bom))

        # 4. Large Digest with > 4096 bytes of file list before first FILE marker (e.g. 150 files)
        lines = ["Directory structure:"] + [f"  pkg/module_{i}/sub/handler_file.go" for i in range(160)]
        lines.append("\n================================================\nFILE: pkg/module_0/sub/handler_file.go\n================================================\npackage sub\n")
        large_digest = "\n".join(lines).encode("utf-8")
        self.assertGreater(len(large_digest), 4096)
        self.assertTrue(is_existing_digest(large_digest))
        self.assertTrue(is_existing_digest(b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + large_digest))

        # 5. Normal text file mentioning Directory structure in comment/body
        normal_code = b"// Some header\nDirectory structure:\nFILE: test\n======"
        self.assertFalse(is_existing_digest(normal_code))

        # 6. Empty data
        self.assertFalse(is_existing_digest(b""))

        # 7. Random python file
        py_code = b"import os\nprint('hello')\n"
        self.assertFalse(is_existing_digest(py_code))

    def test_is_binary_file(self):
        # Text file with ASCII
        txt_path = self.root / "file.txt"
        txt_path.write_text("Hello World", encoding="utf-8")
        self.assertFalse(is_binary_file(txt_path))

        # UTF-16 LE text file (has null bytes in ASCII range, but valid text)
        utf16_path = self.root / "script.ps1"
        utf16_path.write_bytes('Write-Host "Hello"'.encode("utf-16"))
        self.assertFalse(is_binary_file(utf16_path))

        # Real binary file (contains null bytes without UTF-16 BOM)
        bin_path = self.root / "program.exe"
        bin_path.write_bytes(b"\x4d\x5a\x90\x00\x03\x00\x00\x00\x04\x00\x00\x00")
        self.assertTrue(is_binary_file(bin_path))

    def test_decode_text_preserves_characters_and_normalizes_endings(self):
        # 1. UTF-8
        raw_utf8 = "func Main() {\n\tprintln(\"Hello\")\n}\n".encode("utf-8")
        self.assertEqual(decode_text(raw_utf8), "func Main() {\n\tprintln(\"Hello\")\n}\n")

        # 2. Windows CRLF normalization
        crlf_bytes = b"Line 1\r\nLine 2\r\nLine 3\r\n"
        decoded = decode_text(crlf_bytes)
        self.assertNotIn("\r", decoded)
        self.assertEqual(decoded, "Line 1\nLine 2\nLine 3\n")

        # 3. Windows-1252 / Latin-1 copyright symbol \xa9 and em-dash \x97
        cp1252_bytes = b"/* Copyright \xa9 2026 UniCompute \x97 All rights reserved. */\n"
        decoded_cp1252 = decode_text(cp1252_bytes)
        self.assertIn("©", decoded_cp1252)
        self.assertIn("—", decoded_cp1252)
        self.assertNotIn("\ufffd", decoded_cp1252)

        # 4. UTF-16 LE with BOM
        utf16_bytes = "Write-Host 'UniCompute Worker'\n".encode("utf-16")
        decoded_utf16 = decode_text(utf16_bytes)
        self.assertEqual(decoded_utf16, "Write-Host 'UniCompute Worker'\n")

    def test_clean_notebook_content(self):
        sample_nb = {
            "cells": [
                {
                    "cell_type": "code",
                    "source": ["import math\n", "print(math.pi)"],
                    "outputs": [{"output_type": "stream", "text": ["3.14159\n"]}],
                    "execution_count": 5
                },
                {
                    "cell_type": "markdown",
                    "source": ["# Analysis"]
                }
            ],
            "metadata": {},
            "nbformat": 4,
            "nbformat_minor": 2
        }
        # Standard UTF-8 JSON
        raw_bytes = json.dumps(sample_nb).encode("utf-8")
        cleaned, was_cleaned = clean_notebook_content(raw_bytes)
        self.assertTrue(was_cleaned)
        cleaned_json = json.loads(cleaned)
        code_cell = cleaned_json["cells"][0]
        self.assertEqual(code_cell["outputs"], [])
        self.assertIsNone(code_cell["execution_count"])
        self.assertEqual(code_cell["source"], ["import math\n", "print(math.pi)"])

        # UTF-8 with BOM JSON notebook
        raw_bom_bytes = b"\xef\xbb\xbf" + json.dumps(sample_nb).encode("utf-8")
        cleaned_bom, was_cleaned_bom = clean_notebook_content(raw_bom_bytes)
        self.assertTrue(was_cleaned_bom)
        cleaned_bom_json = json.loads(cleaned_bom)
        self.assertEqual(cleaned_bom_json["cells"][0]["outputs"], [])

    def test_discover_project_files_inclusions_and_exclusions(self):
        # Create allowed files
        (self.root / "pkg" / "compute").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.root / "pkg" / "compute" / "node.go").write_text("package compute\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "cmd" / "app").mkdir(parents=True)
        (self.root / "cmd" / "app" / "main.go").write_text("package main\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "README.md").write_text("# Readme\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / ".gitignore").write_text("*.exe\nbin/\n", encoding="utf-8")

        # Create excluded directory files
        (self.root / ".git").mkdir()
        (self.root / ".git" / "config").write_text("git config", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "bin").mkdir()
        (self.root / "bin" / "tool.sh").write_text("echo bin", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / ".tmp").mkdir()
        (self.root / ".tmp" / "temp.go").write_text("temp", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "ui_extracted").mkdir()
        (self.root / "ui_extracted" / "mockup.html").write_text("<html></html>", encoding="utf-8")

        # Create excluded extension and file patterns
        (self.root / "test.exe").write_bytes(b"\x4d\x5a\x00\x00")
        (self.root / "report.docx").write_bytes(b"PK\x03\x04")
        (self.root / "archive.zip").write_bytes(b"PK\x03\x04")
        (self.root / "GEMINI.md").write_text("agent prompt", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "digest.txt").write_text("old digest", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / ".DS_Store").write_bytes(b"junk")

        discovered = discover_project_files(self.root, output_path="digest.txt")
        self.assertIn("cmd/app/main.go", discovered)
        self.assertIn("pkg/compute/node.go", discovered)
        self.assertIn("README.md", discovered)
        self.assertIn(".gitignore", discovered)

        # Ensure exclusions are absent
        self.assertNotIn(".git/config", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("bin/tool.sh", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn(".tmp/temp.go", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("ui_extracted/mockup.html", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("test.exe", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("report.docx", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("archive.zip", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("GEMINI.md", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn("digest.txt", discovered)
        self.assertNotIn(".DS_Store", discovered)

    def test_include_ui_flag(self):
        (self.root / "ui_extracted").mkdir()
        (self.root / "ui_extracted" / "mockup.html").write_text("<html></html>", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "main.go").write_text("package main", encoding="utf-8")

        # Without include_ui
        discovered_default = discover_project_files(self.root, include_ui=False)
        self.assertNotIn("ui_extracted/mockup.html", discovered_default)

        # With include_ui
        discovered_ui = discover_project_files(self.root, include_ui=True)
        self.assertIn("ui_extracted/mockup.html", discovered_ui)

    def test_pack_project_end_to_end_with_multi_encoding_and_utf16(self):
        (self.root / "pkg").mkdir()
        (self.root / "pkg" / "a.go").write_text("package pkg // Line 1\r\n// Line 2\r\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "cmd").mkdir()
        (self.root / "cmd" / "main.go").write_text("package main // Main\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (self.root / "script.ps1").write_bytes("Write-Host 'Hello from PS'\r\n".encode("utf-16"))
        (self.root / "license.txt").write_bytes(b"/* Copyright \xa9 2026 UniCompute. */\n")
        (self.root / "binary.dat").write_bytes(b"ELF\x00\x01\x02\x00some_binary_bytes")

        out_file = self.root / "output_digest.txt"
        res = pack_project(self.root, output_target=out_file)

        self.assertEqual(res["total_discovered"], 5)
        self.assertEqual(res["included_count"], 4)
        self.assertEqual(len(res["skipped"]), 1)
        self.assertEqual(res["skipped"][0], ("binary.dat", "binary"))

        self.assertTrue(out_file.exists())
        content = out_file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

        # Verify no raw carriage returns in output (normalized line endings)
        self.assertNotIn("\r\n", content)

        # Verify directory structure
        self.assertIn("Directory structure:", content)
        self.assertIn("  cmd/main.go", content)
        self.assertIn("  license.txt", content)
        self.assertIn("  pkg/a.go", content)
        self.assertIn("  script.ps1", content)

        # Verify contents and encodings
        self.assertIn("FILE: cmd/main.go", content)
        self.assertIn("package main // Main", content)
        self.assertIn("FILE: license.txt", content)
        self.assertIn("/* Copyright © 2026 UniCompute. */", content)
        self.assertIn("FILE: script.ps1", content)
        self.assertIn("Write-Host 'Hello from PS'", content)

    def test_pack_project_prevents_recursive_digest_packing_with_arbitrary_names(self):
        (self.root / "code.py").write_text("print('test')\n", encoding="utf-8")

        # 1. First packing into an arbitrary name (NOT digest.txt)
        custom_digest1 = self.root / "repo_snapshot_v1.txt"
        pack_project(self.root, output_target=custom_digest1)
        self.assertTrue(custom_digest1.exists())

        # 2. Second packing into another arbitrary name
        custom_digest2 = self.root / "repo_snapshot_v2.txt"
        res2 = pack_project(self.root, output_target=custom_digest2)

        # custom_digest1 MUST be recognized by content as an existing digest and skipped!
        self.assertNotIn("repo_snapshot_v1.txt", res2["included_files"])
        self.assertIn(("repo_snapshot_v1.txt", "prior_digest"), res2["skipped"])
        self.assertEqual(res2["included_files"], ["code.py"])

    def test_max_file_size_cap(self):
        (self.root / "small.txt").write_text("small file", encoding="utf-8")
        # Create a 300KB file
        (self.root / "large.txt").write_text("x" * (300 * 1024), encoding="utf-8")

        out_file = self.root / "digest.txt"
        # Set max size to 200KB
        res = pack_project(self.root, output_target=out_file, max_file_size_kb=200)

        self.assertIn("small.txt", res["included_files"])
        self.assertNotIn("large.txt", res["included_files"])
        self.assertTrue(any(s[0] == "large.txt" and "oversized" in s[1] for s in res["skipped"]))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

## 1. Architecture Overview & Binaries

UniCompute integrates distributed volunteer compute, storage, and cross-platform hardware acceleration across three primary objectives:
- **Objective 1 (P2P Transport & Storage Substrate)**: Dual-stack ICE, CGNAT RFC 6598 hole punching, blind contributor relay fallback, WebRTC SCTP multiplexing (`dc-ctrl` and `dc-bulk`), and content-addressed storage (CAS) disk vault with SHA-256 scrub auditing.
- **Objective 2 (Isolated Compute Engine)**: Air-gapped Docker container execution (`--network none`, `--memory 128m`, `--cpus 1.0`, `--read-only`, dropping all capabilities), remote shell execution, and language runtimes (C/C++, Python).
- **Objective 3 (Cross-Platform GPU Acceleration & Governance)**: Hardware probing (DirectX 12 / DirectML, CUDA, DXGI, NVML), 50 ms battery/activity watchdog preemption, Win32 JobObject memory limits, CUDA-to-AMD HIPIFY analysis & translation, and ONNX training checkpoint persistence.
- **Desktop GUI Control Room**: A standalone desktop app featuring a 60 FPS HTML5 Canvas topology engine (central mainframe tower, orbiting dual-hemisphere workstation rigs, glowing P2P laser beams) and 4 dedicated control panels.

The project compiles into the following binaries in the `bin/` directory:

| Binary | Description |
|---|---|
| `bin\unicompute-gui.exe` | **Desktop GUI Control Room**. Full interactive topology canvas, telemetry dials, peer connection drawer, and panels for Objectives 1, 2, and 3. Protected with cryptographic session token auth and strict loopback Origin checks. |
| `bin\unicompute-node.exe` | **Contributor Peer Node Daemon & CLI**. Manages local CAS vault, WebRTC SCTP connections, Docker sandbox execution, remote shell (opt-in + allowlist), and GPU acceleration. |
| `bin\unicompute-coordinator.exe` | **Signaling Hub & Embedded TURN Server**. Relays WebSocket SDP offers/answers, ICE candidates, and fleet registry. Protected via cluster auth tokens (`-auth-token`) and duplicate node ID hijacking rejection. |
| `bin\unicompute-relay.exe` | **Contributor Relay Daemon (Deprecated)**. Legacy byte relay fallback; modern deployments rely on native Pion ICE and embedded/external TURN. |
| `bin\verify-obj3.exe` | **Objective 3 Automated Hardware Verification Suite**. 7-point validation suite for physical GPU, watchdog, sandboxing, and simulated ONNX execution. |

**Live Deployment**: A production coordinator is hosted and live on Render at:
`wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws`

**Desktop GUI Launchers**:
- Batch Launcher: `.\run-gui.bat`
- PowerShell Launcher: `.\run-gui.ps1`
- Master Verification Suite: `.\test_all.ps1`

## 2. Prerequisites Installation on Windows 10/11

Ensure your computer has:
- Windows 10 (Build 19041+) or Windows 11 (64-bit).
- Hardware Virtualization enabled in BIOS/UEFI (Intel VT-x or AMD-V).
- At least 8 GB RAM and 15 GB available disk space.

Open **PowerShell as Administrator** for all installation commands below.

### 2.1 Git for Windows
Install Git using Windows Package Manager (`winget`):

```powershell
winget install --id Git.Git -e --source winget
```

*Alternative*: Download the official installer from [git-scm.com/download/win](https://git-scm.com/download/win) and accept default settings (enabling Git from the command prompt and Git Bash).

Verify installation:
```powershell
git --version
# Expected: git version 2.40+ or newer
```

### 2.2 Go Programming Language (1.22+)
Install Go using `winget`:

```powershell
winget install --id GoLang.Go -e --source winget
```

*Alternative*: Download the MSI installer from [go.dev/dl](https://go.dev/dl/).

Restart your PowerShell terminal to reload `$env:Path`, then verify:
```powershell
go version
# Expected: go version go1.22+ or go1.23+ windows/amd64
```

### 2.3 Docker Desktop with WSL2 Backend
Worker nodes execute untrusted user code in isolated Linux containers. Docker Desktop backed by Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL2) is required.

#### Step 1: Install or Update WSL2
In Administrator PowerShell:
```powershell
wsl --install --no-distribution
wsl --update
wsl --status
```
*(If prompted, reboot your PC to finish enabling the Virtual Machine Platform feature.)*

#### Step 2: Install Docker Desktop
```powershell
winget install --id Docker.DockerDesktop -e --source winget
```
*Alternative*: Download installer from [docker.com/products/docker-desktop](https://www.docker.com/products/docker-desktop/).

#### Step 3: Configure Linux Container Mode
1. Launch **Docker Desktop** from the Start Menu.
2. Complete the initial setup wizard, selecting **Use the WSL 2 based engine**.
3. Right-click the Docker whale icon in the Windows notification area (system tray).
   - If the menu shows **"Switch to Windows containers..."**, Docker is already in **Linux container mode** (Correct).
   - If it shows **"Switch to Linux containers..."**, click it to switch to Linux mode.
4. Verify Docker daemon access from PowerShell:
```powershell
docker version
```
Look for:
```text
Client: Docker Engine
 OS/Arch: windows/amd64
Server: Docker Engine - Community
 OS/Arch: linux/amd64
```

### 2.4 GPU Drivers & Acceleration Runtime (DirectML / CUDA)
For Objective 3 GPU acceleration and telemetry:
- **DirectX 12 / DirectML**: DirectML is pre-installed on Windows 10 (version 1903+) and Windows 11. It provides hardware acceleration across NVIDIA, AMD Radeon, and Intel Arc GPUs without requiring vendor-specific SDKs.
- **NVIDIA GPU (CUDA)**: Install the latest NVIDIA Game Ready or Studio Driver (v535+). Verify CUDA driver support:
  ```powershell
  nvidia-smi
  # Look for CUDA Version: 12.x or 11.x in the top right header
  ```
- **AMD Radeon (HIP/ROCm)**: For AMD devices on Windows, UniCompute uses DirectML as the primary hardware acceleration target, bypassing ROCm Linux-only driver constraints.

### 2.5 Browser Runtime for Desktop GUI Window (Edge / Chrome)
The Desktop GUI Control Room launches as a borderless native application window using:
- **Microsoft Edge** (installed by default on Windows 10/11: `C:\Program Files (x86)\Microsoft\Edge\Application\msedge.exe`).
- **Google Chrome** (alternative: `C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe`).
No external Electron or WebView2 runtime installation is required—the native browser app engine is used directly.

## 3. Windows Security, Code Signing & Smart App Control

Windows 11 introduces strict security protections including **Smart App Control (SAC)**, **Windows Defender SmartScreen**, and **Execution Policies** that require deliberate handling during local development.

### 3.1 PowerShell Execution Policy
By default, Windows blocks script execution (`.ps1`). Configure your session to allow running project scripts:

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Force
```
*Note*: `-Scope Process` affects only the current PowerShell window and leaves system-wide security settings intact.

### 3.2 Unblocking Downloaded Files
If the repository was downloaded as a `.zip` archive from GitHub via a web browser, Windows stamps files with an NTFS `Zone.Identifier` stream (Mark of the Web), causing SmartScreen to block them.

Unblock all files recursively:
```powershell
Get-ChildItem -Path . -Recurse | Unblock-File
```

### 3.3 Authenticode Code-Signing (`build.ps1`) & Smart App Control (SAC)
On Windows 11 with Smart App Control (SAC) enabled in "Enforce" mode, unsigned local executables or newly compiled binaries lacking cloud reputation may trigger:
```text
Program 'unicompute-node.exe' failed to run: An Application Control policy has blocked this file
```

The UniCompute `build.ps1` script automatically signs compiled binaries by:
1. Detecting or generating a dedicated self-signed code-signing certificate in `Cert:\CurrentUser\My`.
2. Applying an Authenticode signature (`Set-AuthenticodeSignature`) to all compiled `.exe` files in `bin\`.

To manually create a certificate and sign any custom binary:
```powershell
$cert = Get-ChildItem Cert:\CurrentUser\My -CodeSigningCert | Select-Object -First 1
if (-not $cert) {
    $cert = New-SelfSignedCertificate -Type CodeSigningCert -Subject "CN=UniCompute Dev" -CertStoreLocation "Cert:\CurrentUser\My"
}
Set-AuthenticodeSignature -Certificate $cert -FilePath .\bin\unicompute-node.exe
```

### 3.4 Zero-Friction Developer Execution (`go run`)
If Windows 11 Smart App Control (SAC) blocks local standalone binaries because the self-signed root certificate is not in the system's trusted root store, you can run the UniCompute node directly using the Go toolchain:
```powershell
go run ./cmd/unicompute-node [arguments...]
```
Because `go.exe` is signed with established Microsoft reputation, running via `go run` executes without triggering SAC Application Control blocks.

### 3.5 Temporary Execution Directory (`GOTMPDIR`) & Unit Testing
When running `go test`, Go writes temporary test runner binaries to `%TEMP%` (e.g. `signaling.test.exe`). On Windows 11 with SAC, these unsigned temporary test binaries are blocked from running in `%TEMP%` or `.tmp`.

**Recommended Solution**: Always use the included `run_tests.ps1` verification script:
```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\run_tests.ps1
```
`run_tests.ps1` compiles each package's test binary directly into `bin\`, signs it with an Authenticode certificate, and executes it cleanly.

## 5. Running the Automated Master Verification Suite (`test_all.ps1`)

UniCompute provides a unified 30-point master test automation suite covering all Go packages, physical GPU hardware, 50 ms watchdog radar, standalone samples, and GUI REST/WebSocket endpoints:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\test_all.ps1
```

### What is verified (30 Tests Across 5 Phases):
1. **Phase 1: Subsystem Unit Tests (12 Go Packages)**:
   - **`pkg/blobstore`**: Atomic chunk persistence, SHA-256 validation, quota enforcement, bit-rot scrub audit, traversal prevention.
   - **`pkg/codeexec`**: Bounded code request/response framing, 12 KiB source and 4 KiB stdin ceiling checks.
   - **`pkg/gpu`**: Hardware probe (NVIDIA RTX 4050 / DirectML / CUDA / NVML discovery).
   - **`pkg/gpu/hipify`**: Static AST analysis, 32-thread warp blocker detection, and CUDA-to-HIP AST translation.
   - **`pkg/gpu/onnx`**: Model checkpoint serialization, SHA-256 state hashing, interruptible preemption loop.
   - **`pkg/instrumentation`**: Prometheus metrics counters and histograms.
   - **`pkg/nat`**: RFC 6598 CGNAT detection (`100.64.0.0/10`), dual-stack STUN probing, and Hyper-V/WSL adapter pruning.
   - **`pkg/relay`**: Syncthing relay-v1 end-to-end byte proxying and embedded TURN server lifecycle.
   - **`pkg/remoteshell`**: Windows PowerShell command execution and timeout enforcement.
   - **`pkg/signaling`**: WebSocket registration, keepalive tickers, and client message dispatch.
   - **`pkg/transport`**: WebRTC PeerConnection, 16 MiB SCTP receive buffer, and dual DataChannels (`dc-ctrl` and `dc-bulk`).
   - **`pkg/node`**: End-to-end chunk exchange and **Invariant CP-1 (Data Plane Independence)**.
2. **Phase 2: Objective 3 Physical Hardware & Governance Suite**:
   - `cmd/verify-obj3`: 7-point live test suite validating physical GPU detection, Win32 JobObject memory ceiling, 50 ms battery/idle watchdog preemption, and checkpoint rollback.
3. **Phase 3: Standalone Sample Executions (10 Files Individually Verified)**:
   - `samples/c/hello.c` (compiled via native MSYS2 GCC 16.1 -> FNV-1a hash verification).
   - `samples/cpp/fib.cpp` (compiled via MSYS2 G++ 16.1 -> 45 Fibonacci steps and Golden Ratio convergence).
   - `samples/python/calc.py` (executed via Python 3.11 with `samples/python/input.txt` -> 32 records processed).
   - `samples/security/timeout_test.py` (infinite loop bounded by runtime timeout cap).
   - `samples/gpu/portable_vector_add.cu` (standalone HIPIFY -> 7 replacements to portable HIP C++).
   - `samples/gpu/warp_reduction.cu` (standalone HIPIFY -> quarantined under `EXECUTE_NVIDIA_ONLY`).
   - `samples/gpu/inline_ptx.cu` (standalone HIPIFY -> quarantined under `REJECT_RECOMMEND_ONNX`).
   - `samples/gpu/test_model.json` (ONNX capsule parsing, weight loading & SHA-256 checkpoint seal).
   - `samples/security/network_leak_test.py` (air-gap socket probe protocol encapsulation).
   - `samples/security/mem_limit_test.py` (128 MB RAM capping audit protocol encapsulation).
4. **Phase 4: Desktop GUI Daemon & API Verification (Port 23098)**:
   - Validates live `/api/status`, `/api/gpu`, `/api/samples`, `/api/gpu/hipify`, `/api/storage/put`, `/api/storage/scrub`, `/api/gpu/run`, and HTML5 Canvas bundle serving (`GET /`).
5. **Phase 5: Collation & Scorecard Generation**:
   - Outputs a clean terminal table summarizing 30/30 passed tests.

## 7. Running a 2-Node Cluster on Windows

To experience the full peer-to-peer distributed system, open **two separate PowerShell windows**:
- **Window 1 (Worker Node B)**: Enables Docker sandbox code execution, contributes storage, and serves code execution requests.
- **Window 2 (Client Node A)**: Connects to Node B, transfers files into the CAS vault, issues shell commands, and submits jobs.

> [!NOTE]
> **Coordinator Architecture & Authentication**:
> - The Coordinator (`unicompute-coordinator` or the live Render cloud deployment) is a **headless signaling hub and embedded TURN server**. It intentionally has **no standalone web GUI**, as volunteer compute networks require zero overhead on the signaling plane.
> - **Cluster Authentication (`-auth-token`)**: When exposed on non-loopback addresses, the coordinator enforces cluster secret token authentication to prevent unauthorized signaling, node hijacking, and enumeration. Pass `-auth-token <secret>` or set `UNICOMPUTE_AUTH_TOKEN`. (For offline local testing without authentication, pass `-insecure-no-auth`).
> - **Verifying Coordinator Health via API**:
>   ```powershell
>   # Health & Uptime Check (Live Render):
>   curl.exe -s https://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/health
>   # Discovered Fleet Registry (add Bearer header if auth is enabled):
>   curl.exe -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/api/nodes
>   # Local Coordinator:
>   curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
>   curl.exe -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/api/nodes
>   ```
> - **Visualizing the Coordinator in the Desktop GUI**: The visual representation of the coordinator lives inside the **Desktop GUI Control Room** (`unicompute-gui.exe`). When you launch the GUI, **Tab 1: P2P Topology Mesh** renders the coordinator as the central glowing mainframe tower, dynamically surrounded by orbiting worker rigs.

### Option A: Public Live Coordinator on Render
Both nodes connect over the Internet via the production coordinator on Render (`wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws`).

#### Terminal 1 — Start Worker Node B
```powershell

# Method 2 (Go Toolchain - Use if Windows SAC blocks standalone binary):
```

### 8.2 Content-Addressed Storage (CAS) Vault

The CAS vault provides cryptographically verified, quota-enforced local storage.

#### 1. Store a local file in the vault (`put`)
```text
> put samples\python\input.txt
```
*Output:*
```text
Successfully stored blob: 66a2cbdb7d04a60155609462eec4c5fa33f3801ea558b8d960f5e1ef2ecbfcb6 (200 bytes)
```
*(Copy your returned SHA-256 hash for the next steps).*

#### 2. List stored blobs (`list`)
```text
> list
```
*Shows all blobs stored locally, their exact byte size, and modification timestamp.*

#### 3. Inspect blob metadata (`stat`)
```text
> stat <blobID>
```
*Shows size, modification timestamp, and verified SHA-256 digest.*

#### 4. Transfer blob over WebRTC DataChannel to Node B (`transfer`)
```text
> transfer node-B <blobID>
```
*Output on Node A:*
```text
Transferred blob 66a2cbdb... to node-B in 42ms
```
*Output on Node B:*
```text
[EVENT] Chunk 66a2cbdb... (200 bytes) received from peer node-A and stored
```

#### 5. Fetch blob from Node B (`fetch`)
Pulls a chunk from Node B over WebRTC DataChannel using the wire protocol `DataMsgChunkRequest` (0x10), writes it to the local CAS vault, and verifies its cryptographic SHA-256 hash:
```text
> fetch node-B <blobID>
```
*Output:*
```text
Fetching chunk 66a2cbdb... from peer node-B...
[EVENT] Chunk 66a2cbdb... fetched and stored successfully in 38ms (SHA-256 Verified).
```

#### 6. Export blob back to a local file (`get`)
```text
> get <blobID> exported_data.txt
```
*Exports the blob to `exported_data.txt` and verifies byte integrity.*

#### 7. Audit Vault for Bitrot (`scrub`)
```text
> scrub
```
*Output:*
```text
Scrub complete: all stored blobs passed cryptographic SHA-256 verification.
```

#### 8. Delete a blob from vault (`del`)
```text
> del <blobID>
```

---

### 8.3 Remote Terminal Execution (`exec`)

UniCompute provides secure host terminal command execution over WebRTC DataChannels using PowerShell on Windows targets.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Security Gate — Opt-In & Peer Allowlist Required**:
> Remote shell execution is **disabled by default** to prevent unauthorized command execution by connected peers.
> - The target node (Worker Node B) **must** be launched with:
>   `-enable-remote-shell -shell-allowlist <peerID>[,<peerID>]` (or `-shell-allowlist "*"`).
> - If remote shell is disabled or the calling peer is not allowlisted, the request is immediately rejected with:
>   `remote shell disabled on this node` or `peer not in shell allowlist`.

#### 1. Execute command on Worker Node B
```text
> exec node-B hostname
> exec node-B whoami
> exec node-B Get-Process
```
*Output:*
```text
[EXEC] Executing 'hostname' on remote PC 'node-B'...
=================================================================
 Remote Node: node-B | Exit Code: 0 | Duration: 45 ms
 --- STDOUT ---
 DESKTOP-WORKER-B
=================================================================
```

#### 2. Broadcast command to all connected peers
```text
> exec all Get-Date
```

---

### 8.4 Air-Gapped Docker Sandbox Code Execution (`run`)

The `run` command reads a local source file on the client machine, packages it into a bounded job envelope, and sends it over the WebRTC `stream` DataChannel to the worker. The worker executes the code in an isolated Docker container with:
- **`--network none`**: Disables network access (air-gapped).
- **`--read-only`**: Read-only container root filesystem.
- **`--memory 128m --memory-swap 128m`**: 128 MB RAM ceiling.
- **`--cpus 1.0`**: CPU capped at 1 core.
- **`--pids-limit 64`**: Fork-bomb mitigation.
- **`--cap-drop ALL`**: Drops all Linux kernel capabilities.
- **`--security-opt no-new-privileges:true`**: Prevents privilege escalation.
- **`--tmpfs /tmp:rw,nosuid,nodev,size=64m`**: Ephemeral memory-only scratch space.

---

### 8.5 Objective 3: GPU Acceleration & Resource Governance

Objective 3 adds hardware acceleration discovery and background student governance. When running `unicompute-node.exe`, activate GPU support using:

```powershell
.\bin\unicompute-node.exe -id node-A -signaling wss://unicompute-coordinator.onrender.com/ws -enable-gpu -gpu-backend auto -gpu-mem-limit-mb 2048 -gpu-watchdog-poll-ms 50
```

#### Node Flags for GPU Subsystem:
| Flag | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `-enable-gpu` | `false` | Activates DXGI/NVML/DirectML/CUDA hardware detection, 50 ms watchdog, and Win32 JobObject sandbox. |
| `-gpu-backend` | `auto` | Preferred compute backend: `auto`, `directml`, `cuda`. |
| `-gpu-mem-limit-mb` | `2048` | Hard commit memory limit enforced via Win32 JobObject. |
| `-gpu-watchdog-poll-ms` | `50` | Watchdog polling interval for AC power and student keyboard/mouse idle monitoring. |
| `-gpu-ignore-battery` | `false` | Ignore battery state (useful for lab machines or desktop test rigs). |

#### Interactive CLI Commands for GPU:
1. **`gpu`**: Probes and displays real-time hardware telemetry and watchdog radar:
   ```text
   > gpu
   ======================= Objective 3: GPU Hardware & Governance =======================
    Device Name:        NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4050 Laptop GPU
    Vendor:             NVIDIA
    Total VRAM:         6141 MB (6.00 GB)
    Available VRAM:     5920 MB
    Driver Version:     32.0.15.9282
    GPU Temperature:    45.0 °C | Power: 7.9 W
    DirectML Support:   true (DirectX 12 feature level verified)
    CUDA Support:       true
    Backends Detected:  [CPU DirectML CUDA]
   --------------------------------- 50 ms Watchdog State ---------------------------------
    Watchdog Status:    running
    Power Source:       OnBattery=false (100% remaining)
    User Activity:      Active=false (Idle: 12m40s | Sustained Idle: 12m40s)
   =======================================================================================
   ```

2. **`hipify <file.cu>`**: Analyzes CUDA kernels for 32-thread warp assumptions (`threadIdx.x % 32`, `__shfl_down_sync`), inline PTX assembly, and translates portable kernels to HIP C++:
   ```text
   > hipify samples\gpu\portable_vector_add.cu
   [SUCCESS] Kernel successfully translated to portable HIP C++ (7 replacements made).
   ```
   If warp blockers are detected (e.g. `warp_reduction.cu`):
   ```text
   > hipify samples\gpu\warp_reduction.cu
   [BLOCKED] cannot safely translate to HIP: 2 fatal compatibility issue(s) detected
    * Line 4: Hardcoded modulo 32 indexing assumes 32-thread warp size.
    * Line 9: NVIDIA 32-thread warp synchronous intrinsic does not map to AMD 64-thread wavefronts.
   ```

3. **`gpu-run <c|cpp|onnx> <file> [batches]`**: Executes workloads governed by Win32 JobObject memory ceilings and `IDLE_PRIORITY_CLASS`.
   *(Note: The pure-Go ONNX runner is an educational simulation/mock labeled `Simulated: true` that validates checkpoint serialization, preemption loops, and SHA-256 state hashing without requiring external CGO/ONNX Runtime C-bindings).*

### 9. Sample Programs & Security Boundary Tests

The repository includes ready-to-use sample programs in the `samples\` directory. You can use the existing files directly or create them using the PowerShell commands below.

### 9.1 Python Data Processing with Stdin (`calc.py` & `input.txt`)
Reads numbers from standard input, calculates mean, standard deviation, median, min, and max, and outputs descriptive statistics.

#### Creation Commands:
```powershell
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path "samples\python" | Out-Null

Set-Content -Path "samples\python\input.txt" -Value @'
128.50 94.20 15.00 482.10 39.40 88.00 12.34 500.00
73.15 62.40 81.90 190.25 45.60 99.10 312.80 5.40
23.70 87.65 142.10 67.89 44.55 98.70 215.30 63.20
11.45 78.90 34.50 156.70 89.20 45.10 120.00 67.50
'@

Set-Content -Path "samples\python\calc.py" -Value @'
#!/usr/bin/env python3
import sys
import math

def process_stream():
    numbers = []
    print("==================================================")
    print("   UniCompute Worker: Python Data Processing Job  ")
    print("==================================================")
    raw_input = sys.stdin.read()
    if not raw_input.strip():
        print("[WARN] No input received on stdin. Generating default test data.")
        numbers = [42.0, 17.5, 88.2, 9.1, 104.6, 55.0, 31.4, 76.9]
    else:
        for token in raw_input.split():
            try:
                numbers.append(float(token))
            except ValueError:
                pass

    if not numbers:
        print("[ERROR] No valid numbers found in input stream.")
        return

    n = len(numbers)
    total_sum = sum(numbers)
    mean = total_sum / n
    variance = sum((x - mean) ** 2 for x in numbers) / n
    std_dev = math.sqrt(variance)
    min_val = min(numbers)
    max_val = max(numbers)
    sorted_nums = sorted(numbers)
    median = sorted_nums[n // 2] if n % 2 != 0 else (sorted_nums[n // 2 - 1] + sorted_nums[n // 2]) / 2.0

    print(f"Records Processed : {n}")
    print(f"Sum               : {total_sum:.4f}")
    print(f"Mean (Average)    : {mean:.4f}")
    print(f"Median            : {median:.4f}")
    print(f"Standard Dev      : {std_dev:.4f}")
    print(f"Minimum Value     : {min_val:.4f}")
    print(f"Maximum Value     : {max_val:.4f}")
    print(f"Sorted First 5    : {sorted_nums[:5]}")
    print(f"Sorted Last 5     : {sorted_nums[-5:]}")
    print("==================================================")
    print("Status: Calculation completed successfully.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    process_stream()
'@
```
